📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A day after Amazon MGM revealed Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond, Amazon founder and chairman Jeff Bezos said that the was “heavily involved” in the decision.

When speaking at ‌Semafor’s Silicon Valley and the World conference on Tuesday, per Variety, Bezos noted that his team was initially “slightly biased” against Pattinson “because he’s already so famous.” He added, “We sort of thought, you know, maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown.” However, during the rigorous screening tests it became “so obvious.” When referring to Pattinson, Bezos said, “He is James Bond.”.

Industry observers note that the billionaire remarked that the final decision was made last Friday and that they had narrowed a large group down to five finalists who went through “real, old-fashioned screen tests.” The process involved full costumes, real sets, and other actors with the finalists, said Bezos, who called all five actors gunning for the coveted role “amazing.” He added, “But there was something special about Rob and his performance. It was immediately undebated. Denis [Villeneuve], the director … we all gravitated toward Rob.”.

In a recent development, in 2022, Amazon acquired MGM Studios. However, the Bond series’ longtime producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson still retained a significant hold on the direction of the franchise. It wasn’t until last February that Amazon MGM struck a deal with Broccoli and Wilson that would allow them to retain the intellectual property rights to Bond, while giving Amazon MGM Studios full creative control. The legendary spy franchise is among the longest-running and most lucrative in Hollywood history. The last Bond film, No Time to Die, was released in 2021, with that movie capping off Daniel Craig’s five-movie run as 007. Pattinson is set to work with filmmaker Denis Villeneuve, who was revealed as the next Bond director last year. There’s still no firm timeline for when Villeneuve’s Bond movie will go into production and when it will be released.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • EXCLUSIVE: The Unofficial Bridgerton Musical creators Abigail Barlow and Emily Bear have another shortform project on the way.
  • Industry observers note that the pair have penned the score for To Die For Love, an original musical micro-series co-produced by Ampersand and TikTok.
  • “Making To Die For Love has been one of the most rewarding creative experiences of our careers,” Barlow and Bear remarked in a statement to Deadline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: The Unofficial Bridgerton Musical creators Abigail Barlow and Emily Bear have another shortform project on the way.

Industry observers note that the pair have penned the score for To Die For Love, an original musical micro-series co-produced by Ampersand and TikTok. Barlow wrote the script with Jane Austen’s Period Drama‘s Julia Aks. The series will premiere on December 21 on TikTok and PineDrama.

“Making To Die For Love has been one of the most rewarding creative experiences of our careers,” Barlow and Bear remarked in a statement to Deadline. “We love a pressure cooker, and building an entire musical in under five months proved that meaningful storytelling isn’t about time—it’s about the story and the people bringing it to life. We’re endlessly grateful to our extraordinary partners at Ampersand as well as Knockout Shorts for turning this into something beyond what we imagined.” Related Stories News TikTok Creator Videos Coming To Disney+ In December As Hulu Integration Takes Full Effect Legal Google, TikTok And Meta Sue To Block California's Social Media Law That Restricts Addictive Features For Children.

In a recent development, to Die for Love follows an ambitious half-witch vying for her coven’s crown. When she falls for a mortal, their romance takes an unexpected turn, forcing an impossible choice between family and the love of her life. Watch on Deadline.

The series stars Barlow (SIX) and Derek Klena (Savannah Bananas, Moulin Rouge) as star-crossed lovers, and features Anna Maria Perez De Tagle (Hannah Montana, Camp Rock), TikTok star Jess Val, Amy Manford (Phantom of the Opera), Kelsie Watts (SIX, Moulin Rouge), Jalen Thurman (Swolemates), Ceci Balagot (Girl Meets World, Monster High), Davied Morales (Sorry We’re Dead), Cayman Cardiff (Fated to My Homeless Billionaire Alpha, The Billionaire’s Fake Wife) and Heather Dubrow (RHOC).

To Die for Love also marks the return of Barlow and Bear after the duo’s creative journey introduced on TikTok with an original song inspired by Shonda Rhimes’ Bridgerton. The song eventually sparked The Unofficial Bridgerton Musical, which was written, recorded, produced, and engineered independently in just six weeks with lead vocals by Barlow and orchestration, production and additional vocals by Bear. It earned a 2022 Grammy Award for Best Musical Theater Album, and they were the youngest winners ever in the category.

The pair followed up that success with songs for the animated feature Moana 2. They are the youngest composers in history to write all the songs for an animated Disney film, and the first female writing team to do so, collaborating with Mark Mancina and Opetaia Foa’i to craft the sounds of Motonui and beyond.

It has been revealed that “TikTok has a passionate community of musical fans, and we’ve seen how talent like Barlow & Bear can build audiences and fandom on the platform,” Dawn Yang, Global Head of Entertainment & Micro-series at TikTok, remarked in a statement. “Bringing them back with To Die For Love is a natural fit. It speaks to the evolution of musical theater fandom, where stories and communities can originate on TikTok just as they do on Broadway stages.”.

Added Agnes Chu, CEO of Ampersand: “Barlow & Bear are one of our favorite songwriting duos, and To Die For Love showcases what happens when we partner world-class creativity with TikTok. Together with a 125-person union cast and crew in Los Angeles, we are bringing original musical storytelling from imagination to vertical screen at unprecedented speed.”.

All 81 episodes of To Die For Love will be exclusively available on TikTok and PineDrama on December 21. The original soundtrack will be released by Atlantic Records.

Recent findings suggest that executive producers of To Die For Love are Agnes Chu, Benj Pasek, Justin Paul, Danielle Perelman, Chris Crema, Matthew Ko and Kevin Weaver. The production is directed by Paul Becker (Julie and the Phantoms, LEGO’s Heartlake The Musical). Filming for To Die For Love took place in Los Angeles. Knockout Shorts is the physical production partner.

For Atlantic Records, Noah Hubbell serves as executive music producer and Cynthia Meng as music director, with all tracks produced by Emily Bear, Abigail Barlow, Noah Hubbell, and Grant Steller, and mixing and mastering by Jay Marcovitz.

  • Rap star Rod Wave has been indicted on felony drug and weapons possession charges in Georgia.
  • It has been revealed that according to the Fulton County indictment obtained by Rolling Stone, the 28-year-old artist unlawfully possessed Oxycodone and had a gun “within arm’s reach” when he was pulled over for reckless driving on Nov.
  • A lawyer for Wave did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rap star Rod Wave has been indicted on felony drug and weapons possession charges in Georgia.

It has been revealed that according to the Fulton County indictment obtained by Rolling Stone, the 28-year-old artist unlawfully possessed Oxycodone and had a gun “within arm’s reach” when he was pulled over for reckless driving on Nov. 7, 2025. The indictment alleges Wave, whose legal name is Rodarius Green, was driving at least 15 miles over the posted speed limit and disregarded a “traffic control device” in a “highly residential area” of Atlanta along Defoor Ave. The indictment was returned Oct. 30 and unsealed this month.

A lawyer for Wave did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

According to recent reports, green was originally booked on reckless driving and drug and gun possession charges and released the following day, according to online jail records. He allegedly had a black .40 caliber Glock with a high-capacity magazine in his waistband when he was taken into custody, according to Atlanta News First.

It has been revealed that the arrest came the same day Green earned his first-ever Grammy nomination, for Best Song Written for Visual Media, for his track “Sinners” from the 2025 film of the same name. He and his fellow nominees lost the award to “Golden” from KPop Demon Hunters at the February ceremony. In a statement shared with Rolling Stone at the time of Green’s arrest, defense lawyers Drew Findling, Marissa Goldberg, and Zack Findling mentioned the Florida musician was “unjustly profiled and unlawfully arrested.” They claimed the arresting officer was part of the Atlanta Police Department’s “controversial Crime Suppression Unit — a group known for its aggressive tactics and emphasis on high arrest numbers rather than genuine public safety.”.

Sources indicate that the statement continued: “Mr. Green was targeted as part of this quota-driven approach, a practice that undermines justice and erodes community trust. We look forward to vigorously challenging this baseless arrest and the clear violations of Mr. Green’s rights in court.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday is still a couple of weeks away, with the big shopping event falling on November 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday sale is already bringing some worthwhile discounts on Soundcore's Nebula projectors. Prices start at $299 for the compact Nebula P1i and go up to $2,799 for the premium X1S 4K laser projector, with savings of up to $700 across the models we've rounded up. There's quite a bit of variety here, too, from battery-powered projectors you can take camping or move between rooms to more powerful 4K models designed for a dedicated movie-night setup.

The Soundcore Nebula P1i is down to $299 from $399, while the Nebula P1 is $699.99, down from $799. Both offer 1080p resolution and Google TV, but their speaker setups are what make them interesting. The P1i has two 10W speakers that flip out and rotate to direct sound toward your seating area, while the P1's speakers detach completely and can run wirelessly for up to 20 hours. The P1 is also brighter at 650 ANSI lumens versus the P1i's 380, though you'll need a power outlet for either projector since neither has a built-in battery.

Small enough to slip into a bag, the Nebula Capsule 3 and Capsule 3 Laser are worth considering if you want something you can easily take on trips or move around the house. The standard Capsule 3 is down to $399 from $529, saving you $130, while the Laser version is $649.99, down from $749.99. Both offer 1080p resolution, automatic image adjustments, and up to 2.5 hours of battery life, although the Laser model is a little brighter at 300 ANSI lumens compared with the standard model's 200.

Taking movie night outdoors is a little easier with a battery-powered projector, and both the Nebula Mars 3 Air and Mars 3 are designed for just that. The smaller Mars 3 Air is down to $519.99 from $599.99, offering 1080p resolution, 400 ANSI lumens of brightness, and up to 2.5 hours of playback. The larger Mars 3, now $899.99 from $999.99, steps things up with 1,000 ANSI lumens, up to five hours of battery life in Eco mode, and a more powerful 40W speaker. It also has a weather-resistant design that's useful for camping or backyard screenings, though its extra bulk might make it less convenient to carry around.

Industry observers note that if you're ready to move beyond 1080p, the Nebula Cosmos 4K SE at $1,099.99 (originally $1,299.99) offers a more affordable way to get 4K resolution. Its hybrid LED and laser light source delivers up to 1,800 ANSI lumens, while its Dolby Vision support helps bring out more detail in compatible movies and demonstrates. You also get Google TV and automatic image adjustments for easier setup, though it doesn't have a built-in battery, so you'll need a power outlet nearby.

According to recent reports, at the premium end of Nebula's lineup, the X1 and newer X1S are designed for a more serious home theater setup. The X1 is down to $2,299 from $2,999, saving you $700, while the X1S is $2,799 from $3,299. Both use triple-laser technology with 4K resolution, Dolby Vision, and optical zoom, but the X1S has a considerable advantage in brightness, reaching up to 6,000 ANSI lumens compared with the X1's 3,500. That extra brightness is useful in rooms with some ambient light, but the tradeoff is louder fan noise.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: Imax has promoted a pair of executives to newly created roles as it expands its leadership.

Giovanni (Gio) Dolci was named the significant screen exhibitor’s first chief operating officer, reporting to CEO Rich Gelfond. The executive, presently based in London as EVP and chief commercial officer, will transfer to New York with expanded oversight of Global Theatres and Technology in addition to his current leadership of the Global Sales, and Streaming and Consumer Technology teams.

Sources indicate that he’ll serve as a key day-to-day strategic partner for Gelfond. Related Stories News Imax CEO Wades Into 'Cliff Booth' Debate: "Frankly, I Don't Understand" News 'The Odyssey' Powers Record Q3 For Imax, Stock Jumps, CEO On Platform's "Power And Potential".

According to recent reports, dolci joined Imax in 2012 as managing director of Europe and Africa and chief sales officer. Previously, he was Director of Business Development and Commercial Operations at Arts Alliance Media and worked in film financing in the U.K., Italy and Newly introduced Zealand. Watch on Deadline.

“Imax is a stronger, more global business than ever, and we continue to evolve and grow our leadership team to capture the many opportunities ahead,” said Gelfond. “Gio has a deep understanding of our business, our partners, and our people at every level. He’s been central to our growth for more than a decade, and his leadership will be critical in this next era of success.”.

Recent findings suggest that imax also promoted Mark Welton, presently President, Imax Global Theatres, to the newly created role of President, Strategic Partnerships, also reporting to Gelfond. Welton will lead partnerships outside Imax’s core theatrical business, working closely with the manufacturer’s content team on initiatives across sports, events, and consumer brands.

It has been revealed that the 30-year Imax veteran has led theater operations and key partner relationships worldwide including the NHL, MLB and NBCUniversal, which partnered with Imax to show the opening ceremony of the 2024 Paris Olympics. “Mark has been instrumental in building IMAX, and few people know our manufacturer and industry like he does,” said Gelfond. “He is exactly the right person to turn the strength of our brand into new sources of growth.”.

Imax has been on a tear over the past few years as PLFs and event cinema became a key part of the post-Covid theatrical experience for consumers and studios. The company reported strong quarterly earnings earlier this month powered by The Odyssey.

Mulaney stopped by Jimmy Kimmel Live to discuss his latest stint on SNL and his latest film Madden, and revealed that he recently produced a collection of songs for his stepfather-in-law’s country band, Sam and the Pink Notes.

After sharing a story about his own father, Kimmel asked Mulaney about his relationship with Sam Schmid, the stepdad of Mulaney’s wife Olivia Munn.

It has been revealed that “Sam, Olivia‘s stepdad, came into their lives a few decades ago,” Mulaney noted. “He’s a wonderful man. He is a retired eye doctor. Sam, since I’ve known him and came into Olivia’s life about five years ago, I’ve always heard him play these songs that he’s written.”.

Recent findings suggest that mulaney explained that Schmid had written a lot of songs with his camping club in the 1970s. “He’d written all these songs over the years, so for Christmas I got him a recording studio in Chicago, and we made an album of those original songs,” Mulaney said, explaining that he found many of the band members who played with Schmid on the album.

Kimmel asked why the album, titled Oldskeedad, isn’t at the moment available to purchase anywhere. “I got a lot going on,” Mulaney replied. “I’m the manager and I’m currently the record label and the record producer. This is an enormous conflict of interest.”.

It has been revealed that it was actually Kimmel’s idea to bring Sam and the Pink Notes onto the late-night show as a musical guest. He and Mulaney discussed the possibility after Mulaney’s Wrigley Field comedy show in July. 10 Reveals Like 'The Traitors' You Should Watch Next

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1349 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that what started as De Verraders way back in 2021 has become a global reality phenomenon: Peacock in the U.S.
  • Recent findings suggest that A reality show with a complex history as relates to The Traitors, the premise being so similar that it may well have served as an inspiration.
  • If there were a prize for dramatic title (and set design), you could do a lot worse than this one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that what started as De Verraders way back in 2021 has become a global reality phenomenon: Peacock in the U.S. hosts the American version with the sartorially supreme Alan Cumming, and also the earlier UK take as well as iterations from Australia, Canada, and New Zealand—but there are spin-offs in France, India, Germany, Ireland, Turkey, and more. Basically, throw a dart at a map and you're likely to hit a country with its own take on The Traitors. And yet! The addictive nature of reality TV means that we can't really ever get enough. In that spirit, here's more backbiting reality TV, and a couple of dramas that offer up similarly duplicitous thrills.

Recent findings suggest that A reality show with a complex history as relates to The Traitors, the premise being so similar that it may well have served as an inspiration. Here, players participate in collaborative missions in order to build a prize fund. But it's not all fun and games: There's a secret double agent among the group (the mole, obviously) whose sole task is to undermine the ability of the rest of the group to earn money. Eliminations are done via quiz: The group is grilled on the information they've collected about the mole, and whoever knows the least gets the boot. Originally airing in the aughts, Netflix brought it back for a couple of seasons more recently, with the potential for more to come. Stream the most recent seasons of The Mole on Netflix.

If there were a prize for dramatic title (and set design), you could do a lot worse than this one. In this South Korean reality show, 12 celebrity contestants are challenged to build a prize pot through strategy games. Sometimes they're collaborative, sometimes entirely competitive, and sometimes a blend, but prizes come in the form of "Pieces" that can be won or lost (and that eventually combine to create their own final puzzle). Anyone who finds themselves without a single Piece is out. Pieces can be spent to buy advantages, and also traded, so the show turns on players forming alliances in order to build the prize pot and survive as long as possible. Stream The Devil's Initiative on Netflix.

Industry observers note that here, a bunch of strangers are holed up in an apartment building, cut off from the outside world—and each other. Players can only interact via a custom app, and, thus, can portray themselves however they want, whether that means being 100% genuine (unlikely!) or creating a whole newly introduced persona. Players judge the competition based on their interactions, determining the "Influencers" who will get to decide on the eliminations. The show ran for seven seasons on Netflix, and is moving to Hulu for the forthcoming eighth. Stream The Circle on Hulu.

Recent findings suggest that you show up at a fancy hotel, and someone hands you a suitcase containing one million dollars. It's yours to keep—as long as you can keep it a secret. In this one, all the contestants get a suitcase, and only one contains the money. Much as with The Traitors, the goal is to figure out who's keeping the secret, with challenges designed to help flush that person out. If the truth is discovered via a vote, that former millionaire is ousted and the money is concealed in another suitcase until the final contestants are given the opportunity to swap bags with someone who they think has the money. Easy come, easy go, I guess. Stream Million Dollar Secret on Netflix.

In a recent development, I'm a little more into the normies on Traitors myself, but there's no question that a big part of the appeal (for most seasons) is watching reality-show celebs go at it with cash on the line. So it is with House of Villains, a Big Brother-style competition with Joel McHale as ringmaster. The core premise is pretty simple: villains (Richard Hatch, Tom Sandoval, Jonny Fairplay, one-time Trump bestie Omarosa Newman, etc.) compete in challenges for rewards and for safety from the inevitable banishment. It's all mostly an excuse to watch some of TV's biggest personalities go for each other's jugulars. Stream House of Villains on Peacock.

According to recent reports, this is not a reality show, but rather a drama about a reality show that may well slake your thirst for treachery while offering up consequences a bit more dramatic than the bruised egos and hurt feelings of The Traitors. Here, eight strangers are selected to compete in a game in which they're locked together in a building and sequestered on different floors each night. They earn money for each minute they last in the game, but all their provisions must be purchased with money they've won, at an extreme markup. At first, the contestants pool their resources so that everyone gets more money—until they learn that people on higher floors are getting more. Then things get nasty Stream The 8 Show on Netflix.

This one plays a bit like The Traitors in reverse: A $250,000 prize pot is, right off the bat, allocated to all 11 contestants who get to hang out in a luxurious villa. So the game isn't about winning money so much as it is about how much you'll keep and how much you're willing to share. Eliminations offer the opportunity to remove those who the others don't want to share with—though contestants don't have to actually ever vote anyone out. They can just keep their portion of the money and hang out, something that obviously does not happen. Challenges along the way force contestants to reveal embarrassing and sometimes ugly truths about themselves that may well put them on the outs with the others. There's only one season at present, though there's potential for more. Stream The Trust on Netflix.

According to recent reports, blending the Significant Brother-esque social aspects of Traitors with Survivor's love of the great outdoors, this one drops four teams of four into the Alaskan wilderness (moving to Panama for season three). The contestants are all, by inclination, loners, but the game has only one core rule: Only a team (of at least two) can win, so while the game has the typical reality show eliminations, these wilderness enthusiasts must work together in order to take the money. In the same way that The Traitors creates a tension between competition and cooperation via its communal prize pot, Outlast sees its contestants forced to maintain relationships whether they like it or not. Stream Outlast on Netflix.

Industry observers note that the tasks on Traitors aren't typically the most thrilling part of the show, which makes this James Bond-branded competition a solid match if you want more complicated and better developed challenges. In this one, nine teams of two visit exotic locations in each episode and compete in spy-themed activities with the ultimate goal of winning £1 million by making it to the end. It leaves out the bits where people sit around a castle strategizing, but it includes, like Traitors, a dapper Scotsman not afraid to camp it up—in this case, Brian Cox, serving as the spymaster who directs the teams in their missions. Stream 007: Road to a Million on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that squid Game: The Challenge would probably be a more reasonable choice for this list—given that it's a proper reality show and not a blood-chilling thriller. But I'm sticking with the original drama here since, as perfectly entertaining as that spin-off is, it feels like it misses the point. In the original (surprise smash hit) drama, 454 needy contestants are recruited for a fresh reality competition in which they're tasked to play rather simple children's games—with deadly consequences that are cheered on by the wealthy financiers who are willing to pay good money to watch both the poors go at each other, as people turn on each other to survive and to win the rather shockingly large prize. A bit like The Traitors if all of Alan's murder schtick were literally true. Stream Squid Game on Netflix.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Winners of the IDFA Forum prizes were revealed at an awards ceremony in Amsterdam Wednesday, honoring projects presented in the festival’s co-production and co-financing market.
  • How Love Moves by Pallavi Paul won the Al Jazeera Documentary Co-Production Award, which comes with a $25,000 prize.
  • Jurors Mohamed Elmongy and Brigid O’Shea wrote of How Love Moves, “As the selectors of the Al Jazeera Co-Production award we took carefully into consideration the urgency and relevance of each selected project for IDFA Forum as well as the aesthetic, artistic, and creative qualities they hold.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Winners of the IDFA Forum prizes were revealed at an awards ceremony in Amsterdam Wednesday, honoring projects presented in the festival’s co-production and co-financing market.

How Love Moves by Pallavi Paul won the Al Jazeera Documentary Co-Production Award, which comes with a $25,000 prize. The award recognizes projects “addressing an urgent glitch of our time, presented in the Pitch or Roundtable categories.” How Love Moves is no stranger to the festival: it received IDFA Bertha Fund support through the IBF Classic scheme, in the Development category in 2024 and the Production and post-production category in 2025. Related Stories Documentary Cinephil Boards Alexandru Solomon's Romanian Election Doc 'Small Expectations' - IDFA Documentary IDFA Artistic Director Isabel Arrate Fernandez On Festival's Competition Lineups, "Huge" Interest In Elizabeth Holmes Doc, And AI In Documentaries.

Jurors Mohamed Elmongy and Brigid O’Shea wrote of How Love Moves, “As the selectors of the Al Jazeera Co-Production award we took carefully into consideration the urgency and relevance of each selected project for IDFA Forum as well as the aesthetic, artistic, and creative qualities they hold. We unanimously agreed to give this award to a politically and creatively sophisticated project, exploring the vulnerability of communities deemed dangerous and wrong through state-inflicted violence. In doing so, we believe audiences around the world will have access to a place and the people living there who otherwise we may never encounter, and correct or add a new layer of complexity beyond the mainstream narrative. And more importantly, it is an exciting opportunity to support a woman-director’s voice, we hope at a critical junction in the life of her project.” Watch on Deadline.

The ARTE European Talent Development Award, recognizing a project in development or early production presented in the Forum’s Pitch or Roundtable categories, went to Stitch by Stitch by Alina Baitokova. That award comes with a €10,000 prize.

Recent findings suggest that jurors Olga Chernykh, Anne-Laure Négrin, and Hanne Phlypo said of Stitch by Stitch, “We were honored to be invited on the jury and listen to so many powerful stories from around the world. We had a long jury deliberation, and many projects were highly appreciated. We recognized the incredible courage of the filmmakers bringing us these stories. If we could, we would have awarded more, and we hope these projects will find their way to be supported, and maybe already found support here at the international market of IDFA.”.

It has been revealed that the jurors continued, “However, as we needed to pick only one project, we decided to award a project from a country whose stories are rarely told, with high need in support right now, and to give a director tools to move the project ahead and tell the story that shows people struggling for their life in a rarely seen part of the globalization. It’s a film brought by a promising team, a delicate emerging voice. Therefore, the jury decided to award a film that takes us to Kyrgyzstan, Stitch by Stitch directed by Alina Baitokova, produced by Adilet Karzhoev and Marianna Kaat.”.

The award for Best Pitch Project comes with a €1,500 prize.

The award for Best Roundtable Project is accompanied by a €1,500 prize.

In other IDFA Forum prizes, the award for Best Rough Cut Project went to Resisting Residents by Nikos Pilos and Arsinoi Pilou.

Sources indicate that “Resisting Residents is a powerful reminder of how cinema can champion what we believe in,” wrote remarked jurors Chalida Uabumrungjit and Cleo Veger. “This brave documentary captures a community standing firm for their homes, their dignity, and their right to live together, proving that film can be an essential voice for justice and human solidarity. We were moved by the courage of the residents, who take in newcomers, face their own conflicts and fight eviction together, and by a film team honest enough to show all of it. Shot by a two-person crew living inside the community, it’s close, trusting and alive, and we can’t wait to see it finished.”.

The award comes with a €1,500 prize.

Resisting Residents also won the InVision Subtitling Award, presented by Walter Groenewegen, which provides closed captioning and subtitles for a project presented in the Rough Cut category.

The IDFA DocLab Forum Award for Best Project was claimed by This Pleasant Lady by Victoria Mapplebeck. “The jury unanimously agrees that this project is inspirational and addresses serious subjects in an irreverent but impactful way that will engage with audiences no matter of their cultural background or ages. The spirit of the project and the artist fits the vibe of IDFA DocLab. We’re also now encouraged to create our own fuck you list!” remarked jury members Min-Wei Kuo and David Massey.

The award is accompanied by a €1,500 prize.

Sources indicate that jurors additionally recognized Time Hunter XR: Colonial Protocols by Mark Mushiva and Daniel Chein. “The jury want to give a Special Mention to a project that really thinks carefully about how the experience will take audiences on a journey that explores themes of time travel, sci-fi, and embodied archive. The project creates an imaginative and engaging experience that brings forward the perspectives of people whose voices deserve to be heard, and histories that deserve to be told.”.

#27793. Five Things I Wish I'd Known Before Getting a Foldable Phone

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1354 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Five Things I Wish I'd Known Before Getting a Foldable Phone

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1354 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the iPhone Duo might be the highest profile foldable phone to date, but it’s by no means the first.
  • Recent findings suggest that one of the most notable aspects of the iPhone Duo is how wide its screen is, even while closed.
  • In a recent development, compare with my Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which features an extremely tall 2.17:1 aspect ratio when closed, but a nearly square 1:04:1 aspect ratio when open.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the iPhone Duo might be the highest profile foldable phone to date, but it’s by no means the first. Personally, I’ve had my eye on the Google variant, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold—and recently I finally took the plunge. I thought I’d done my research to know how different having a foldable phone would be, but I still had a bit to learn. Here are some of the things I wish I’ve learned along the way after making the jump to foldables.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most notable aspects of the iPhone Duo is how wide its screen is, even while closed. And there’s a good reason for that: The larger screen while open has exactly the same 1.41:1 aspect ratio as the smaller screen while closed. This has a ripple effect on how every app you use looks and feels—and whether you like Apple’s approach is largely a matter of personal preference.

In a recent development, compare with my Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which features an extremely tall 2.17:1 aspect ratio when closed, but a nearly square 1:04:1 aspect ratio when open. On the outer screen, apps are a little less wide than on my old phone, but there’s plenty of space for reading books or articles on the inner screen.

I like the tall, thin display personally because it feels easier to reach buttons with my thumb, and the wider display is better for reading. However, this approach can occasionally result in some odd app layouts. Not every app is designed for tablets, especially on Android, and shifting the aspect ratio between the inner and outer display sometimes means re-rendering or even restarting an app entirely to load properly.

The iPhone Duo has a more consistent aspect ratio and general feel between the inner and outer display, but it comes at the cost of a really wide phone. Neither approach is better or worse on its own, but it might be worth going to a local store to get your hands on the phone you’re thinking about before buying.

It has been revealed that for years, the screens on most smartphones have been made of increasingly tough and scratch-resistant glass. So tough that you might not even need a screen protector anymore. On a foldable phone, that can be true of the outside display, but it’s very much not when it comes to the inner, foldable display.

According to recent reports, screens might be foldable, but the strong, durable glass that makes your phone so scratch-resistant isn’t. No matter what foldable phone you use, the covering on the inner display will be more flexible, and thus softer. Apple uses a nano-texture polymer film that can be replaced, but the film on most foldable phones cannot. That means if they get damaged or scratched, those marks will be there for the life of your phone.

Industry observers note that if you (like me) haven’t considered a screen protector in a while, it might be time to try one again, at least for the inner display. It’s also worth keeping in mind how rough you strategy to be with your phone. Construction sites or factories might not be the best home for a foldable phone you plan to open a lot, but an office job should be a bit safer.

Recent findings suggest that similar to the screen protector issue, cases can be more of a headache. Most rigid cases will come in two pieces, and the piece that covers the outer display can be shockingly minimal—barely more than a frame, for some of the cases I looked at. A poorly made case can be brittle or pop off more easily, so it’s more notable to get a high-quality one.

Recent findings suggest that if you like to use your phone case as your wallet, it’s also key to be wary of cases that aren’t specifically designed for your model of phone (and maybe some that are). A lot of wallet cases are built to unfold to reveal your phone’s screen on one side, and your cards and ID on the other. But depending on how your foldable phone unfolds, it could be awkward to reach the inner screen.

The hinge also introduces more spaces for dust and debris to get into your phone. Despite the extra moving parts and gaps, most foldable phones still offer the now-standard IP68 dust and water resistance rating. That mainly applies to what can get inside and damage the components inside your phone. It’s still possible for hair and dirt to get gummed up in any pinchable spaces, so look out for any case that might provide even more nooks for dust to collect in.

Industry observers note that I’ve set up most of my apps how I like them by now, but when I first got my foldable phone, I had to revisit some settings I thought I was done messing with. One of the most notable examples was my ebook apps: I was previously using a single-column, medium-font layout, but it looked ridiculous on the inner display. After switching to a two-column layout, it not only felt more natural, but a lot like reading a regular book.

In a recent development, similarly, there were some uses for my calendar app that got a whole lot more useful. I’ve never really been able to use anything other than either the one-day or Schedule view if I want to make out anything, but on the inner screen, I can finally look at my week at a glance. But that meant tweaking some things—like showing reminders, which fit naturally amid my events in Schedule view, but become a cluttered mess when I saw 14 different reminders to take my meds at once in the Week view.

Most apps do a decent job of automatically adjusting to different screen sizes, but I found a few outliers that I had to figure out myself. As an example, Google Docs would default to a view with extremely tiny text when I first started using it. It took me a bit to figure out that this was due to a “Print layout” toggle in the document’s settings. This is, for some reason, enabled by default when opening a document on the larger inner screen. It can take some time to learn the eccentricities of all your apps, but it’s worth poking around when you can.

Recent findings suggest that I know, it sounds so obvious, right? The outer screen is the one you’ll use most often, so how could you forget about it? But when you unfold the inner screen, the outer one is still useful in some surprising ways that I hadn’t even considered until I went poking around in some of my apps.

One of the most adorable examples is the Made You Look feature in the Pixel’s Camera app. When unfolded, you can take a picture using the rear camera and see a preview like normal, while the outer screen shows silly animations to capture the attention of a baby or toddler that you want to look into the camera. Admittedly, this is an older feature, but it’s a clever one. For adults, you can also use the outer display to get a selfie preview while using the rear-facing camera.

Industry observers note that the outer screen is also just better for some things. YouTube is one of the few apps that has a unique layout designed for a partially folded screen, with the video playing on the tilted-up portion of the screen, and video controls on the bottom portion.

However, in my experience, it was a lot nicer to watch a YouTube video by just propping up the outer screen by unfolding the phone a bit, like a kickstand. My Pixel even detected when YouTube was in full-screen mode on the outer display and would be more forgiving of unfolding the phone without switching to the inner screen. The phone anticipated I might just want to prop up the smaller screen, which I thought was a nice touch.

Alison Doody, who appeared with Ford in Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade, features.

Icons Unearthed: Arnold Schwarzenegger Movies charts the star’s journey from championship bodybuilding to Hollywood, looking at his breakthrough roles, action-film collaborations and move into comedy with Twins and True Lies. It will feature Jesse Ventura, who starred with Schwarzenegger in Predator and The Running Man and similarly went into politics.

Icons Unearthed: Quentin Tarantino Movies explores the filmmaker’s rise from video-store clerk to Oscar-winning Hollywood auteur, along with how his passions for kung-fu and Westerns have influenced his work. The career-spanning series covers Reservoir Dogs, Pulp Fiction, True Romance, Natural Born Killers, From Dusk Till Dawn, Kill Bill, Inglourious Basterds and Django Unchained, and features Bronson Pinchot, who acted in True Romance.

“Our first pop-culture factual series is about going behind the screen to explore how iconic films and franchises took shape,” said David Buoymaster, Chief Investment Officer at Radial, which has a deep catalog of shows of films and shows launched across various platforms.

“Nacelle is the perfect partner to bring that ambition to life through four distinct Icons Unearthed titles, each with the space to tell its own story. From Transformers to the films of Ford, Schwarzenegger and Tarantino, we’re excited for our platform partners and pop-culture fans to discover the creative choices, collaborations and business decisions behind these screen legacies.”.

Industry observers note that “We couldn’t be more thrilled to partner with Radial Entertainment to bring these upcoming seasons of Icons Unearthed to the audience,” added Nacelle CEO Brian Volk-Weiss. “These demonstrates are packed with the kind of brand-new, behind-the-scenes stories and nostalgia fans love, and Radial is the perfect partner to help them reach even more viewers.”.

The deal was negotiated by Katie Carroll, Director, Originals & Business Development at Radial Entertainment, and Hud Woodle, VP International Sales at The Nacelle Manufacturer.

#27789. The Unexpected History of 'Black Friday'

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1209 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

The Unexpected History of 'Black Friday'

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1209 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since the 1950s, Black Friday—once simply known as "the day after Thanksgiving"—has grown into a quasi-holiday in the United States marked by steep discounts, ceaseless shopping, and occasional violence.
  • While pre-dawn trips to the mall are waning as online shopping grows, in-person shopping on Black Friday is still a big deal in the U.S.—it’s estimated that around 80 million Americans visited a brick-and-mortar store on Black Friday in 2025.
  • Sources indicate that “Black Friday” in the United States originally referred to the start of the Panic of 1869, when the collapse of the price of gold devastated the national economy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since the 1950s, Black Friday—once simply known as "the day after Thanksgiving"—has grown into a quasi-holiday in the United States marked by steep discounts, ceaseless shopping, and occasional violence. But more recently, Black Friday has also metastasized. It's not a day anymore. It's a week, a month, a veritable state of mind. (Speaking of which, check out Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage. We got all the deals, baby!).

While pre-dawn trips to the mall are waning as online shopping grows, in-person shopping on Black Friday is still a big deal in the U.S.—it’s estimated that around 80 million Americans visited a brick-and-mortar store on Black Friday in 2025. But how did Black Friday come about, and what does it all mean?

Sources indicate that “Black Friday” in the United States originally referred to the start of the Panic of 1869, when the collapse of the price of gold devastated the national economy. “Black Friday” as a description of the day after Thanksgiving dates back to 1951; the term first appeared in the journal Factory Management and Maintenance, where it referred to the number of employees who skipped work on the day after Thanksgiving. Around the same time, the police in Philadelphia and Rochester started informally using “Black Friday” to describe the traffic and crowds that appeared in their cities as shoppers hit the stores on the day after Thanksgiving. The phrase gradually caught on. It was picked up by national press in 1975 when the New York Times used "Black Friday" specifically to describe the day after Thanksgiving and the shopping and sales it brings.

According to recent reports, but even before it had a name, Black Friday was a thing. The day after Thanksgiving has been known by merchants as the start of the shopping season since the late 1800s. By the early 20th century, retailers sponsored Thanksgiving Day parades that traditionally ended with an appearance by Santa Claus, as if to say, “Now it’s time to shop for Christmas.” By unspoken agreement among retailers, Christmas-themed advertisements rarely appeared before Thanksgiving in our grandparents’ day. This informal bargain obviously no longer applies.

Referring to a day as “black” traditionally denotes a period of calamity or tragedy, leading some to suggest different names for the day. In the early 1960s, Philadelphia merchants suggested “Major Friday,” a name which did not catch on, leaving retailers with the weak explanation that the “black” in Black Friday refers to the black ink denoting profits in a ledger. Oft-repeated lore suggests that retailers are "in the red" all year, and only start making an annual profit at the end of the year, but big retail chains generally make money all year long.

Recent findings suggest that A more modern glitch with the name is that Black Friday sales now last for days or even weeks, beginning in early to mid-November and bleeding over into the following Saturday, Sunday, “Cyber Monday,” Tuesday, and beyond, leading people to say things like, “Do you want to go Black Friday shopping this Sunday?” So far, alternative names like “Five-Day Frenzy” and “The day I get to trample someone to save $8 on a Nespresso” haven’t caught on. But here’s hoping.

Industry observers note that beginning around 2010, an insatiable thirst for profits led many retailers to push the start of Black Friday shopping to Thursday (aka Thanksgiving Day). Kmart opened Thanksgiving morning. Toys R Us opened that night. By 2011, Walmart was opening its doors at 10 p.m. on Thursday. The trend led to widespread backlash, with many Americans appalled that employees were forced to work on Thanksgiving or angry that consumerism was encroaching upon a holiday meant to celebrate colonialism. By 2021, most major retailers had relented and elected to remain closed on Thanksgiving.

Industry observers note that the term “Cyber Monday” describes the boost in online retail sales on the Monday after Thanksgiving, sparked by workers returning to the office and getting right to online shopping. The term first appeared on Nov. 28, 2005, in a Shop.org press release entitled “'Cyber Monday’ Quickly Becoming One of the Biggest Online Shopping Days of the Year," which may be the most influential press release ever written. Since its early 2000s birth, Cyber Monday has become the biggest online shopping day of the year. Americans spent $14.25 billion online on Cyber Monday 2025, according to Adobe Analytics. So is Cyber Monday bigger than Black Friday? Retailers really don't care: Analysts now tend to mash everything into the category of "Black Friday–Cyber Monday" (or even "Cyber Week").

If all this naked consumerism makes you a little squeamish, you're not alone. Anti-consumerists have named the day after Thanksgiving “Buy Nothing Day,” which you can celebrate by doing charity work, cutting up your credit cards, or simply not purchasing anything. Pioneered by artist Ted Dave and popularized by Adbusters magazine, the first Buy Nothing Day was celebrated in Canada in 1992.

It’s hard to measure the success of the alternative holiday. Both online and brick-and-mortar retail sales have increased sharply since 1992, suggesting Buy Nothing Day’s effect is negligible. On the other hand, maybe substantial retailers are losing millions because someone on Bluesky reminded you not to shop. Sure.

Depending on how you measure it, Black Friday has resulted in between one and 17 deaths. Jdimytai Damour is the only person killed directly due to a Black Friday sale: The 34-year-old worker was trampled to death by a surging crowd at a Long Island Walmart on Black Friday in 2008. If you include car accidents, shootings, retail worker suicides, and fatal heart attacks, Black Friday’s death toll balloons to 17, with 128 reported injuries.

Black Friday violence has even inspired a horror flick: Eli Roth's 2023 holiday-themed slasher Thanksgiving opens with a hilariously brutal Black Friday riot at a massive box store, setting off a chain of events that involve a lot of people being murdered by a dude in a Pilgrim mask.

In a recent development, I mean, yeah, of course. Critics of Black Friday point out that there are arguably better times to buy a newly introduced TV (like the week before the Super Bowl), not to mention plenty of other goods. Savings from Black Friday shopping are often illusory—massive-ticket “doorbuster” items generally sell out promptly, leaving behind goods that are, by and large, priced the same as they would be at any other time of year. Some retailers even mark up products ahead of Black Friday so the discounts look bigger. If you're buying online, your browser history, location, and cart contents can tweak the prices you see on Black Friday, as they can on any other day.

Yet despite protest holidays, the unpleasantness of shopping when stores are overcrowded, and the frustration of hunting for bargains that often aren't that great to begin with, Black Friday stubbornly remains an unofficial holiday, celebrated by over 100 million Americans in one way or another. What that indicates about our country's relationship with capitalism is unclear, but personally, I’m going to continue my own day-after-Thanksgiving tradition of eating pie for breakfast and thinking about going for a walk, but then watching The Quick and the Dead instead. I'm not protesting anything; I just don't need the hassle.

Here’s a quick rundown of my credentials: I shop for a living (seriously, I spend eight hours a day scouring the internet for exciting new products), I’ve tested thousands of different items, and, perhaps most importantly, I’m the daughter of a dad who also happens to be my best friend. It has been revealed that when shopping for Dad, start with his interests. (And if you don’t know what those are, I’m going to assume your sibling is the favorite child.) So, just like he used to tell you during your hockey games, you’d better get moving.

According to recent reports, in short, yes. Though they aren't quite as impactful as they once were, Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales offer discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Whether it's a major purchase you've been saving up for or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts, especially on items like appliances and electronics. Last year's sales included categories such as tech, home improvement, and fitness.

Black Friday used to be when major retailers offered their best deals on expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Now, however, the distinction is almost meaningless: Every major retailer offers sales on both days, which means the smart move is to know what you want, use price trackers to monitor the deals, and refer to our Black Friday coverage, where we do all the searching, curating, and price tracking for you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: We recently unveiled the first Friday the 13th film in nearly two decades — and now, we have new details on the project, which wraps production today.

Industry observers note that the film, directed by the previously confirmed Steve Miner, is titled Jason. It’s slated for a worldwide theatrical release on Friday, August 13, 2027, with Cineverse overseeing its North American distribution.

The ensemble cast is led by Schuyler White (Haunt) as Jason Voorhees, the enigmatic masked murderer at the heart of the slasher series, and Natalie Alyn Lind (Dutton Ranch) as “final girl” Lauren.

It has been revealed that others in the cast include Matt Cornett (Every Year After) as Asher, Lilia Buckingham (Hocus Pocus 2) as Madison, John Owen Lowe (Unstable) as Jake, Summer Madison (The Summer I Turned Pretty) as Emily, Selena Turner (Will Trent) as Olive, Matthew Keoni Sato (High School Musical: The Musical: The Series) as Lucas, Brook Sill (Stranger Things) as Zoe, Guillermo Diaz (Scandal) as Rick, Johnell Young (Wu-Tang: An American Saga) as Frank, Sencere Messiah Brown (Homage) as Chase and Bryan Gael Guzman (Nickel Boys) as Dylan. Watch on Deadline.

White, a stunt coordinator and special effects artist, returns to the role of Jason after playing him in the recent short Sweet Revenge made to commemorate the 45th anniversary of Jason Universe.

On the decision to cast him here, franchise steward Robbie Barsamian told us, “We spent months thinking about how to create the scariest, most imposing Jason and who truly deserved to wear the mask. Beyond his towering physical presence, we knew Schuyler understood what makes Jason tick—and that he had the work ethic and genuine respect for this franchise to get it right. He approached this theatrical feature like the role of a lifetime, packing 30 pounds of solid muscle onto his 6’5″ frame and studying the iconic Jasons who came before him so that he feels like an unstoppable force of nature. On set, we framed him low and tight, so the audience is right there in his space, looking up at him. This will be the most intimidating Jason that has ever been on screen.”.

According to recent reports, on casting Lind — an actress seen on Dutton Ranch, The Goldbergs and Significant Sky — as the franchise’s newly introduced final girl, Barsamian noted, “Natalie is not only an excellent actress and incredibly hardworking, but also one of the biggest horror enthusiasts and fans of this franchise. When you put all that together you get something special. This franchise has had many strong female leads, but her performance might just be the strongest this franchise has ever had.”.

Jason marks the 13th entry of Friday the 13th, an iconic horror franchise that debuted with a namesake 1980 slasher. Working from a script by emerging screenwriter David Fliegel, Miner returned to the director’s chair after introducing Jason’s machete in Friday the 13th Part II and unveiling his hockey mask for the first time in Friday the 13th Part III. The film was made independently to afford the Barsamian family, which financed and produced and control the franchise through their tech giant Horror, Inc., total creative control.

Directed by Sean S. Cunningham, the original Friday the 13th watches as a group of counselors at Camp Crystal Lake, preparing to reopen the summer camp, are stalked and killed by an unseen assailant, while the memory of a boy who drowned there years earlier hangs over the grounds. Produced independently for roughly $550,000 and acquired by Paramount in a bidding war, the film provided the foundation for a durable, low-budget sequel machine, with Paramount releasing early entries and and Warner Bros./New Line joining as distributor from the ’90s on. The original film surprised with the revelation of (SPOILER) matriarch Pamela Voorhees as the murderous antagonist, while later entries embraced the machete-wielding Jason himself as the franchise’s terrifying driving force.

In a recent development, over the decades, Friday the 13th has spawned video games, immersive experiences, comic books, collectibles, apparel and more, alongside the films. Horror, Inc. launched the Jason Universe to usher in a latest era of expansion in the franchise in 2024, and most recently, the franchise has been back in circulation via Crystal Lake, Peacock and A24’s prequel series, which premiered all eight episodes on Oct. 15.

White is repped by Brand in Motion; Lind by CAA, Authentic and Brecheen Feldman Breimer; Cornett by Gersh, LBI Entertainment and Walter Entertainment & Media Law; Buckingham by Buchwald and Industry Entertainment; Lowe by UTA, Untitled and Latham & Watkins; Madison by Formation Talent Agency, Kevin Donahue Management and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller; Turner by Paradigm, Play Management and Forward Talent; Sato by Buchwald and Skrzyniarz & Mallean; Sill by Griffin Talent and Luber Roklin Entertainment; Diaz by Innovative; Young by Eris Talent Agency, Stride Management and Nelson Davis; Brown by Avenue Agency; and Guzman by Formation Talent.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • iOS 27 gave Apple Maps a handful of new features, and my favorite is one that keeps offering fresh updates every week: Local Lists.
  • Recent findings suggest that apple Maps has long offered a ‘Guides’ feature where you can browse curated collections of places worth checking out.
  • But in iOS 27, there’s a new feature—Local Lists—that’s sort of an extension of Guides, but it gets updated weekly with the latest trending places.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27 gave Apple Maps a handful of new features, and my favorite is one that keeps offering fresh updates every week: Local Lists.

Recent findings suggest that apple Maps has long offered a ‘Guides’ feature where you can browse curated collections of places worth checking out. Sometimes they’re created by Apple’s editorial team, other times by celebrities or in conjunction with current events.

But in iOS 27, there’s a new feature—Local Lists—that’s sort of an extension of Guides, but it gets updated weekly with the latest trending places.

Here’s how Apple describes it, via Apple Newsroom:.

With Local Lists, Apple Maps users in the U.S. can find the perfect spot for meeting friends, dining, and more. Using intelligent insights from what’s trending, Maps surfaces locally relevant collections of places — from trending restaurants to great spots to take kids — so it’s easy for users to find what they are looking for. All insights are derived with privacy in mind and never tied to individual users.

Industry observers note that I’ve always enjoyed browsing Guides in Maps to help find new places. But Local Lists are a great expansion of the idea, especially since they’re updated all the time. I’m always up for trying a new trending restaurant, and now Maps makes it easy to stay on top of what’s new.

Even if you’ve been using iOS 27 for months, there’s a good chance you’ve never seen Local Lists. That’s because they’re pretty hidden.

To find the feature, tap into the search field in Maps and scroll down to see a new ‘Trending Restaurants’ section. On my iPhone 18 Pro, by default this section gets hidden behind the keyboard, so you have to first scroll and dismiss the keyboard to see it.

Sources indicate that trending Restaurants are ranked from 1-20. The search screen highlights only a handful, but you can tap to view the full list. For example, if you open the ‘Trending Restaurants in Fresh York’ list, you’ll see 20 places worth checking out.

How does a restaurant make the list? Per the in-app explanation, the list contains “Restaurants climbing in popularity this week, based on what people view, share, and interact with on Apple Maps.”.

Yeah still not my go to navigation option. Until they can give users the amount of information / detail / items to mark and make its alerts functioning like Waze, it won't really be much of a competitor. This stuff if great to have but why Would I want to keep switching between apps to get different information.

Maybe in 3-5 years their engineering team will mimic Waze and treat it like they've just discovered something great😒🤣.

It has been revealed that since these Trending Restaurants lists revision weekly, Apple states you’ll want to save any places you plan to visit. There’s a convenient + button next to each listing.

It’s unclear exactly how many different parts of the US have localized lists in iOS 27. But if you poke around and find the full collection of Local Lists, there are 1,021 total—so you’ll probably have one in your area.

You can browse all available lists by opening a Trending Restaurants list then tapping where you see the Apple logo and ‘Local Lists’ near the text that claims when it was last updated.

Sources indicate that have you used Local Lists in iOS 27’s Maps app yet? Let us know what you think via the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • But a combination of the upcoming Pro controls on the iPhone 18 Pro and a new feature introduced with iOS 27 means there are more times when I can stick to Apple’s stock Camera app.
  • Developers know that a big reason for using third-party camera apps is being able to use them in much the same way you would a standalone camera.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When shooting both photos and videos on my iPhone, I make regular use of a few different third-party apps, mostly because I like to take manual control.

But a combination of the upcoming Pro controls on the iPhone 18 Pro and a new feature introduced with iOS 27 means there are more times when I can stick to Apple’s stock Camera app. If you aren’t already using customizable controls, I highly recommend doing so ….

Developers know that a big reason for using third-party camera apps is being able to use them in much the same way you would a standalone camera. A key part of this is having easy access to manual control over things like aperture (on the iPhone 18 Pro), shutter speed, white balance, and choosing between manual and auto focus. Those settings are right there on the main screen of almost all third-party apps.

According to recent reports, with the iPhone 18 Pro, the same set of controls are also available in Apple’s stock camera app. By default, these are tucked inside a menu, requiring an initial tap to open it. As we noted back in September, however, iOS 27 brings customizable controls to the camera app.

It has been revealed that simply open the menu and tap the Edit button (top-left when holding the phone vertically) and you can add any of the controls to the main screen. This makes them available in a single tap.

For still photography, I have these:.

Sources indicate that aperture, shutter speed, and white balance as these are the three main manual controls I use. Exposure compensation, because sometimes the only reason I want to take manual control is to increase or decrease the exposure, and that provides a faster way of doing so (quicker than the alternative drag up/down within the photo, in my experience). Finally, I have one-tap access to the histogram to help in setting exposure.

It’s a similar story in video mode. I again have aperture and white balance along with exposure compensation and the histogram. But here I add instant access to frame-rate and focus modes (as I’m more likely to switch focus mode when shooting video).

Of course, third-party apps still have an key role, but this one change has made a big difference to me when using the stock camera app for both photos and video.

Recent findings suggest that do you make use of this feature yourself? If so, please share the details in the comments.

Walmart’s early Black Friday sale just kicked off, offering no shortage of worthy tech deals, and one home audio deal in particular has our attention. If you’re looking to level up your home theater audio setup for less, the Vizio 4.1 Pro SV410YW-10 Soundbar and wireless surround speakers setup with Dolby Atmos and DTS:X support is on sale for $79 (originally $148), a nearly 50% discount.

The two pre-paired wireless surround speakers can be positioned behind or beside your seating area, while two bass drivers built into the 32-inch soundbar mean you don’t need a separate subwoofer. The system maxes out at 95 dB, with bass extending to 50 Hz.

Recent findings suggest that the SV410YW-1 connects to your television through HDMI eARC and supports CEC, so you can adjust the volume with your TV remote. #27773. The Man Who Broke the Texas Democratic Party to Save It
