The Man Who Broke the Texas Democratic Party to Save It

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3688 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • T he personal office of Texas Democratic Party Chair Kendall Scudder is a museum to Democrats’ greatest victories, disappointments, close calls, and one-hit wonders.
  • “He’s a crazy motherfucker that guy,” Katherine Fischer, executive director at Texas Majority PAC, quips to me as I sift through boxes of what I estimate to be several thousand vintage (and not so vintage) campaign pins, trying to be mindful of old rusty needles.
  • Sources indicate that buttons reading “UNBEATABLE MONDALE FERRARO,” “SHIRLEY CHISHOLM FOR PRESIDENT,” and “Smile If You Had an Affair with Bill Clinton” flow across the conference table like spilled gold from an overturned pirate’s chest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

T he personal office of Texas Democratic Party Chair Kendall Scudder is a museum to Democrats’ greatest victories, disappointments, close calls, and one-hit wonders.

“He’s a crazy motherfucker that guy,” Katherine Fischer, executive director at Texas Majority PAC, quips to me as I sift through boxes of what I estimate to be several thousand vintage (and not so vintage) campaign pins, trying to be mindful of old rusty needles. “In the best possible way,” she clarifies.

Sources indicate that buttons reading “UNBEATABLE MONDALE FERRARO,” “SHIRLEY CHISHOLM FOR PRESIDENT,” and “Smile If You Had an Affair with Bill Clinton” flow across the conference table like spilled gold from an overturned pirate’s chest. Every available flat plane of space from which something can be hung or displayed in the Dallas office is occupied. A collection of ceramic Jim Beam whiskey decanters shaped like Democratic donkeys lives behind his desk. Ashtrays full of lapel pins dot tables and shelves. An entry table holds a gavel belonging to former House Speaker Sam Rayburn, a true blue son of Texas. Campaign posters for Lyndon Baines Johnson — Scudder’s favorite president — Robert Kennedy, Barbara Jordan, FDR, Hubert Humphrey, Jimmy Carter, Barack Obama, and dozens of others form a crowded gallery wall spanning the length of the room. The closets are stuffed with storage bins containing money stacks of political bumper stickers and rolled poster boards. A “Frances Farenthold for Governor” sign is displayed above the toilet in the bathroom.

It is the lair of a political mad scientist, one whose experiment just came alive.

A Democratic senator from Texas is headed to Washington, D.C. A Democrat is going to be the governor. A Democrat is going to be lieutenant governor. The party also flipped the seats of the attorney general, comptroller, agricultural commissioner, land commissioner, and railroad commissioner. They converted 12 judicial seats from red to blue, took over the board of education for the first time in three decades, and won control of the Texas state House for the first time since 2002. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

According to recent reports, the transformation may feel like an overnight fluke to outside onlookers, with the party riding a wave of anti-Trump sentiment into a generational electoral coup. To think that would require discounting the work of extremely sophisticated candidate campaigns, organizers, and the work Scudder began to ensure that any gains made by Texas Democrats — however marginal — could serve as a foundation rather than a transitory win.

Six-foot-three with a large frame, dark hair, and bright hazel eyes, Scudder can cut a mean figure if he has the inclination to. When he’s not stumping, soliciting, or selling, he can be goofy, prone to bouts of excess energy, and eager to discuss the project he’s thrown himself into over the last 20 months: a radical reconfiguration of the Texas Democratic Party.

As chair of the party, he’s angered longtime fixtures of the state’s political establishment, grated on the political economy of the region, and ultimately — through both accident and intent — placed Democrats in a near-perfect position to meet the moment when lighting finally struck.

It’s now a blue Texas, if he can keep it.

In a recent development, “People kept saying you’re doing too much, too fast, you’re supposed to be a caretaker chair, you’re going to lose all this institutional knowledge,’” Scudder says in his Texarkana brogue that broadcasts his rural roots — when we first met at Terry Black’s Barbecue in Austin. “You’re worried I’m going to ruin the institutional knowledge of what? Losing?”.

Veteran organizers, current as well as former Texas politicians, and advisers described the Texas Democratic Party of their lifetimes as a bloated, Austin-centric social club that did little for candidates, and even less for voters. The party was caught in a cyclical spiral of self-defeatism, and — through a combination of financial and structural factors — unable to retain and grow insurgent waves of voter support like that which boosted former U.S. Rep. Beto O’Rourke’s near-miss in the 2018 Senate race. After the losses of 2024, particularly among Hispanic and Black voters within the state, Lone Star Democrats found themselves in a crisis.

Sources indicate that democrats “thought you could lock a bunch of consultants in a room in Austin and buy your way out of the problem,” Scudder tells me, after (correctly) complaining that charging $50 for a tray of brisket and sides is ridiculous. Scudder, himself from a farming family, does not abide by sacred cows. His first three major actions upon assuming the chairmanship were to move the party headquarters out of the liberal stronghold of Austin to red-ringed Dallas County, clear the debt weighing down their accounts, and overhaul the party’s leadership.

The leadership overhaul almost derailed his tenure just as it began. Top staffers, including the party’s former chief of staff and executive director, resigned after Scudder unveiled they would be required to move to the latest Dallas headquarters, accusing him of wanting to remain in his hometown (the Austin office was converted to a field office). Claims of union-busting and racism were leveled against him by former party employees, two of whom ultimately attempted to unseat him when he ran for a full term in the summer of this year. By then, Scudder had managed to bring enough of the party around to his vision to comfortably secure his reelection to a four-year term.

“When I came in the party had about a third of its precinct chairs full across the whole state, and about 20 percent of our counties didn’t even have a county chair. We needed to rebuild it.”.

Industry observers note that scudder released a widespread organizer and candidate development effort to establish a presence in all 254 Texas counties, the party surged recruitment and pulled in over 100 candidates to fill out downballot races — many of which hadn’t had a Democrat run in years — through the “Texas Challengers” program. For the first time in the party’s modern history, every race had a candidate. Now-outgoing Governor Greg Abbott and his advisers dismissed the effort as a “gimmick” earlier this year. A dozen of them would go on to win.

It has been revealed that texas Democrats staffed up over a thousand county and precinct chairs, and moved to open field offices in Houston, Eagle Pass, and Amarillo. The party rolled out paid civics education classes to boost voter turnout, and enforced a new, equal-opportunity bidding process for campaign consultants and services, negotiating universal rates to save candidates millions in expenditures across the state. They also built the first coordinated campaign in the party’s history, pulling together over $40 million in campaign contributions statewide, including a research consortium available to local candidates typically excluded from the multi-billion-dollar consultant and pollster economy. Fischer, who oversaw the coordinated campaign with Texas Majority PAC, told me that almost immediately after Scudder’s election “we started to build the machine that would be used in 2026,” with limited funds and a lot to prove, the partnership focused on “efficiency and creativity,” to make every dollar work for the party.

The way Scudder and his staff tell it, it was the beginning of a 10-year proposal, maybe five or six if they managed to do every single thing right. To them, a great night in the midterms would have been one that sent James Talarico to the Senate, flipping a few House seats, and maybe even stealing the governorship. Roughly a week before the election, Scudder received a polling patch from the research consortium, predicting blowout wins throughout the state. “I looked up at the team,” he recalled, “and noted ‘fuck the consortium is busted.”.

In early 2025, Scudder invited his wife, Carly — a specialized therapist for foster children — to his office. The couple were expecting their first child later that year, and he had a pitch to make.

On one side of a freestanding dry erase board, he had a bulleted list of “all the things we wanted in a name.” A name that wasn’t weird or exceedingly common, worked with Carly’s mother’s maiden name (Joiner) as a middle name, and ideally a reference to a family name.

It has been revealed that “I walked her through it,” he gushed, reenacting how he flipped over the board for her, and there in large letters was his proposal: LYNDON JOINER SCUDDER — after the 36th president of the United States, a born and bred Texan, and also an amalgamation of her full name — Carolyn — and her father’s name, Don. “We couldn’t name him Don,” he adds in a conspiratorial whisper.

Little Lyndon — now 15 months old and completely unaware of what just happened in his his state — was born last July.

Sources indicate that LBJ clearly looms large for Scudder. He’s not only a symbol of the true power of progressive Texan governance, but of the power elected officials ultimately have to shape the lives of those they govern.

“Johnson’s Great Society pulled my family out from poverty,” he states. Born in East Texas near the not-so-fresh town of New Boston, Scudder’s family carved a path to their American dream on the winds of the Democratic social policies of the 20th century. His grandfather was delivered alone by his mother “in a wash bucket” on the family farm that, as he claims, only had water and electricity because of FDR. The programs of the New Deal and Great Society would rescue the Scudders from the fallout of the Great Depression. His left hand sports a gold wedding band, his right an edgeworn class ring from Sam Houston State University, the word “honor” engraved inside the band. He was the first person in his family to go to college, and it “might as well have been Harvard.”.

“Everything I have in my life is because progressive Democrats,” he insists. “Democrats were the only people fighting for me. I love this party, and to think that Republicans could get elected, get rid of such a rich history of this progressivism in this country, and just run them up the way they did — I have no fucking patience.”.

That patience began to run out at around 12 years old. In the early 2000s Republicans would seize same sex marriage and relationships — in a similar manner as they now treat anti-trans concern — as a supposed social contagion with which to browbeat the opposition. Outgoing Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas), then the state attorney general, defended anti-sodomy laws criminalizing same-sex couples, and the party at large sought to brand LGBTQ individuals as unfit to parent. Scudder, the child of a lesbian couple, took to door knocking in opposition.

He became an organizer for Texas College Democrats and Texas Young Democrats, opening dozens of chapters throughout the state. His own attempts at seeking elected office fell flat — losing a Texas state Senate race to Republican incumbent Bob Hall in 2018, and a Democratic primary to Texas House Rep. John Bryant, a former member of the U.S. House of Representatives, in 2022. It is perhaps a testament to Scudder’s graciousness that Bryant has since become a close friend and adviser, so much so that he officiated his wedding.

Perhaps the most revolutionary thing about Scudder is his lack of cynicism. Losing doesn’t scare him, losers don’t disgust him. “I know where all the landmines are because I’ve stepped on them all,” he jokes at one point as we stand in among his collection of decades of campaign shrapnel. All the names of victors, legends, disappointments, and “what ifs” piled together into a movement he can now shape.

Sources indicate that almost everything in Jim Hightower’s home looks like it was brought into the world by human hands. The ranch-style house in a quiet Austin neighborhood just off of South Congress is full of things that were carved, woven, pinched, molded, and whittled. It’s the kind of lived-in western space the tech transplants of the Austin goldrush pay out the ass for, but never really achieve. Outside, his garden is an untamed tangle of native plants and wildflowers. At 83, he likes that they “basically take care of themselves.” Voters, not so much.

Hightower is a bit of a legend among those who know political ball. As a younger man he worked under Texas Senator Ralph Yarborough — a staunch supporter of integration and civil rights during a time when most Southern senators refused to do so. He founded the progressive newspaper The Texas Observer and served as Texas Agriculture Commissioner between 1983 to 1991 — the last Democrat to hold the office until Clayton Tucker was elected last week. He is now one of the only living members of the last generation of Texas Democrats to serve in statewide elected office — one that held power during a time when the party represented union labor, farm workers, and social and economic advancement for the diverse population of the state.

Sources indicate that “Populism began in Lampasas, Texas. Literally four farmers sitting around a kitchen table saying the banks are screwing us, and the railroads are screwing us, and we’ve got to do something,” he explains to me as we chat on his screened-in back porch. Somewhere along the way, as corporate interest and major money took hold of American politics, “our party quit standing for worker rights, environmentalism as strongly as we had. We still ostensibly stood for it but we lacked conviction and we lacked action, and people noticed that.”.

When Hightower ran for Agricultural Commissioner— alongside future governor Ann Richards, then a candidate for State Treasurer — the candidates ran as a collective ticket, a “unified campaign” that built on their individual constituencies. “They thought they couldn’t win, and here we came,” Hightower recalls. It wasn’t “just one ego, but an actual progressive movement that could change Texas.”.

It has been revealed that it’s a romantic vision of a time long gone, but it rhymes with the Democratic victory of 2026. In the aftermath of 2024, with Texas Democrats once solid multi-racial coalition in shambles, it was clear something needed to change. As the party looked to make inroads in the state in 2026, O’Rourke advised Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa to treat her run as a joint venture with the party’s Senate candidate, arguing that it would be near impossible for a single Democrat to pull off the upset without building a multi-candidate voter coalition. Quality candidates with robust campaigns could make the jump under the right set of circumstances, in the right cycle — but making the party a true competitive force long term would require specialized attention. “We were looking for a party chair who could do something besides sit there in the chair,” Hightower says. Scudder, adept at fundraising and a wunderkind communicator, seemed like a viable choice. “He was willing to fight the bullshit and the bullshitters who were retarding the party, who didn’t seem to even quite understand what the party was and what it could be.”.

The people who work with Scudder will tell you that he’s kind of crazy, a bit gregarious, a font of boundless energy that sometimes needs to be reined in and is smart enough to know it. He will readily hand out his phone number to anyone who asks for it, take any call, respond to whatever request comes from whatever part of the state. Lillian Salerno, a senior adviser to Scudder and former Obama administration official, met him when he was 19 years old.

According to recent reports, after years favoring corporate Democrats, Scudder wanted to create a culture where “when candidates came in, they felt recognized” by the party, Salerno tells me over coffee near the Texas Capitol. She had run and lost a House race in 2018, and knew firsthand how the process feels for a candidate. “It didn’t work out for me — but I didn’t feel like the party gave a shit whether I ran or not,” she says. “Maybe it was just my impression, but I felt like I wasn’t an Austin person, so I didn’t really have a place. If I felt like that, maybe other candidates did too.”.

Scudder’s opening blitz was about as subtle as a gunfight, but it served to (mostly) reset the decayed relationships between the party core and the state at large.

It has been revealed that the party “was always asking me for a contribution, as opposed to doing anything that I felt was particularly meaningful to get me elected,” states Texas House Rep. John Bryant. “Under Kendall, it’s completely different, and a lot of the elected officials are having to come around to this realization.”.

Industry observers note that “In my experience the county chairs of the staff had just clashed endlessly, they couldn’t stand each other,” Terri Burke, the current Executive Director of the party, tells me over Diet Cokes in Scudder’s office, which is separate from the main party headquarters because (as he will readily tell you) he can be a bit overwhelming. “The State Democratic Executive Committee (SDEC), they couldn’t stand the staff. The staff couldn’t stand them. There was so much conflict. There was so much dysfunction.”.

In a recent development, and not just dysfunction, but a refusal to adapt. “We’ve been doing the same old, same old for a long time, but not getting the results that we all of us wanted to see,” claims Texas state Senator Royce West — a power broker and longtime fixture in the Texas political scene. “Yes, there were some controversial decisions that were being made. But here’s the deal: sometimes you’ve got to be a disruptor. And if you’re going to be a disruptor, it has to be done with the purpose. Kendall is the person to do it.”.

As goes Texas politically, so goes America.

Scudder is quite young compared to most of Texas’ Democratic greats. During our first meeting in Austin, Scudder, still a little scrambled by the outcome of election night, mentions that there was not a single living Texas Democratic Party chair who knew how to actually plan a gubernatorial inauguration. He was going to be flying blind.

Getting Gina Hinojosa sworn in is a small task compared to the prepares Scudder is already brewing for 2028 and beyond. Democrats made history, now his job is to retain their control of the state, and ideally expand it.

“I gotta protect all these flips. I gotta flip a couple Senate seats,” he rattles off at one point. “If you think I’m not going after that Senate next cycle you haven’t met me yet.”.

Sources indicate that scudder also intends to do all he can to ensure Democrats govern as Democrats. There’s a lot of talk at the moment of concession-making and what sort of limits Hinojosa and other Democrats should abide by in order to avoid rattling the temporarily dormant Republican coalition in the state. Scudder sees part of his job as ensuring the coalition doesn’t give up the shop.

“We just want to be helpful, but part of that being helpful is understanding that it’s a Democratic governor, and we would expect her to stay as close to the Democratic platform as we could possibly get,” he says. “People got her elected as a Democrat, and we would like for her to govern as such.”.

They’re up against immense challenges. There will not be a major statewide candidate on the ballot in 2028, which means their efforts will be attached entirely to the presidential ticket. Republicans in the state have already broadcast their intent to throw wrenches into Hinojosa’s tenure wherever they can. He will have to convince the national Democratic party that Texas is no longer a state that they can afford to write off.

In a recent development, we are “responsible for a movement” now, he says. Our “job is to grow it.”.

Should he succeed where his predecessors have failed, the implications go far beyond Texas.

One of the first people to call Scudder and congratulate him after election night was Senator Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), who has advised the chair on his organizing efforts, and frequently campaigns on behalf of Texas candidates.

It has been revealed that “As goes Texas politically, so goes America,” Sanders tells me over the phone, noting that the trove of Electoral College votes harbored by the state would make presidential math near impossible for Republicans. “What happened on November 3 is extraordinarily vital, not just for Texas but for America — and Kendall, in a very quiet way, helped make that happen by demanding that there be candidates in every race, every legislative seat in in the state, and by building the kind of grassroots movement that should be built not only in Texas but all over the country.”.

Recent findings suggest that “There is no reason why [Texas] should not be one of the more progressive states in the country,” the senator adds. “It’s a young state, it’s a working class state, large minority populations — there was no rational reason why it was run by right-wing leaders — and I think that’s something that Kendall understood in what he did.”  Trending Stories Watch Buffalo Springfield Come Together for the First Time in Many Years Jennifer Lopez Teases New Music on ‘Fallon’: ‘This Does Feel Like a Happy Era’ The ‘You Can See Everything’ Interview You’ve Been Waiting For Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters Files for Divorce From Fourth Wife Kamilah Chavis After 5 Years of Marriage.

Making Texas a true swing state or returning it to a true blue stronghold, would be the political feat of the century.

Scudder is not taking his eye off the ball. “It’s one thing to burn their house down,” he tells me with a hungry glint in his expression. “But I want to nail their door shut.”.

According to recent reports, this week, Perplexity has deployed its fresh proactive agentic AI feature called Teammates to the Mac. Perplexity Teammates were previously limited to iOS and the web.

Similar to Grok Bot, Perplexity Teammates are task-oriented proactive agentic AI threads that work for you without constantly being prompted. Meta Muse and ChatGPT Dots are similar, but use a single chat model rather than supporting multiple instances.

Here’s more about Perplexity Teammates:.

Teammates are a team of AI agents that own ongoing work. Give a teammate a responsibility, such as managing a growth campaign, triaging incoming bug reports, tracking your metrics, or researching a new market, and it owns that work around the clock. It prepares the tasks, brings in more agents when the work grows, and follows through until the result is ready for your review.

It has been revealed that access to Teammates currently requires a paid Perplexity Max subscription. The feature builds on top of Perplexity’s existing AI orchestration system.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • W hatever you do, do not ask the six musicians in Man/Woman/Chainsaw which one of them is the chainsaw.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

W hatever you do, do not ask the six musicians in Man/Woman/Chainsaw which one of them is the chainsaw.

“Don’t do it,” warns singer Vera Leppänen, looking deadly serious. “We’ve heard that one so many times.”.

“It’s so annoying,” states her bandmate Billy Doyle, shaking his head.

Billy Ward, another bandmate, agrees: “Don’t ask about the name.”.

Luckily, the name is far from the most interesting thing about this fast-rising, fantastically original London group. Their first full-length album, Cannonball, collides all kinds of sounds that really shouldn’t go together — vulnerable folk, head-banging hard rock, a bit of classical, a little dance music, several genuinely enormous pop hooks — and, somehow, it works like a charm every single time. It’s a magic trick that gets more remarkable with every replay. When we saw Man/Woman/Chainsaw play at South By Southwest in March 2025, we called them “a young band in the process of inventing something ecstatically upcoming.” Cannonball is what they invented, and sure enough, it’s one of this year’s most rewarding debuts.

The day after their first-ever Newly introduced York show, the six of them have gathered in the backyard of a coffee shop in Bed-Stuy to chat with Rolling Stone. It’s our second choice for a meeting spot — the first café we tried had no room for a party of seven — but these young musicians are hardly bothered by a last-minute change of location. Leppänen (lead vocals and bass), Ward (lead vocals and guitar), Emmie-Mae Avery (lead vocals and keyboard), Clio Starwood (violin), Doyle (guitar), and Lola Cherry (drums), all aged 21, sit around a table in the sun, lighting rollies, laughing, and trading notes on last night’s gig.

It has been revealed that “It’s funny,” Leppänen notes. “America’s so far away for us, and they know our songs.”.

“The music crossed the pond,” states Starwood.

According to recent reports, “Yeah,” Ward notes. “I walked past some people chatting at the bar, and they were talking about why they were there: ‘So I’m a really significant Chainsaw fan…'” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

It has been revealed that A few hours later, at the second stop on their U.S. tour, they show why their music has drawn such an enthusiastic audience in this country. It’s the night before Halloween, and the club is packed with costumed people who are ready to have fun — and Man/Woman/Chainsaw are more than happy to oblige. Up front, Ward and Leppänen rage like a pair of punk-rock demon twins. He growls theatrically on “The Thing” and “Goddamn, Lizard Man!,” and she slides with ease from the sullen fury of “Still Angry” to the pristine clarity of “Lighter.” Starwood shreds on her violin, Doyle brings a dash of jazzy style on guitar, and Cherry is a tireless dynamo behind the kit. Then there’s Avery, whose mellifluous vocals are indispensable to “Nosedive” — their biggest hit by far, with nearly 2.5 million Spotify plays — and their killer cover of the Breeders’ “Cannonball.” By the end of the night, the whole room is literally jumping.

According to recent reports, man/Woman/Chainsaw have been building toward this moment for about seven years. Ward and Leppänen were the first to meet, crossing paths at age 14 at the BRIT School, the performing-arts laboratory whose alumni include Adele, Amy Winehouse, Lola Young, and Olivia Dean. They spent the next few years assembling a backing band, which wasn’t too hard — “We knew a lot of people that played a lot of instruments,” Leppänen says — and booking gigs at local pubs. Related Content Who Gets to Own Rock & Roll History? No One Writes About Everyday Life Quite Like Star Moles How Bob Dylan’s Trip to London Inspired ‘Girl From the North Country’ Geese Never Thought They’d End Up Here.

“We’d be in school, and Billy and Vera would come up to me at lunch and be like, ‘Do you want to go play the fucking Amersham Arms tonight?'” Avery recalls.

Recent findings suggest that by the time they all turned 16 or 17, they were drawing attention for their wild live performances. (The band name, for the record, appears to be a reference to feminist film critic Carol J. Clover’s influential 1992 volume Men, Women, and Chainsaws, in which she identified the horror trope of the “final girl.”) And though Ward dismisses the music they were making at this point as “just noisy London bullshit,” they found a place in a scene that was regaining its bearings after the end of Covid restrictions.

Sources indicate that “It’s such a privilege to be from a city that has so many venues, that has so many people that champion independent music,” Leppänen claims. “We were very lucky to be able to just go out and do whatever.”.

“We’d be on lineups with crazy noise rock, or post-punky stuff with a guy talking, or really electronic stuff,” Ward says. “There’s just such a variety.”.

“It felt like you could do anything,” Cherry notes.

Man/Woman/Chainsaw’s eclectic sound reflects the band’s democratic writing style, where anyone can make a suggestion and everyone will listen. It’s “the cocktail combination of six brains,” as Starwood puts it. And while many of them are fond of pop acts like Chappell Roan, Olivia Rodrigo, and Lana Del Rey, they see no contradiction between those sounds and the others in their mix.

“A lot of the best rock music, even the artiest, weirdest, guitary-est music, has great pop choruses,” Ward says. “That’s a thing that pretty universally makes the song good, is having something you can come back to. It’s important.”.

According to recent reports, they spent about two years workshopping the songs on Cannonball before stepping into RAK Studios with producers Seth Evans and Margo Broom in the summer of 2025 to begin recording. All the while, most of them were attending university (all but Ward and Avery, who opted to focus on the band). As part of her degree, Leppänen wrote papers on subjects including the Irish rap trio Kneecap, for a class on music and politics. She mentions that she later met one of the members of that group — “I did tell him I wrote about him. He said, ‘You’re welcome.’ And he said I was charming” — which leads her to a story about the time they all ran into Lewis Capaldi at a Chainsaw show. “He said I was a boss,” she states.

Industry observers note that “Both of these people were wasted when they gave these compliments,” Ward observes wryly. “So let’s take it with a pinch of salt.”.

For another graduating requirement, Leppänen submitted a performance by Man/Woman/Chainsaw. “If people want to know if we’re a good band, the answer is yeah, we got a good mark,” claims Starwood.

Sources indicate that some of the songs on the album began with a group jam, like “Only Girl,” the soaring anthem that opens Cannonball. “I just had two chords,” Ward says. “And a dream,” Leppänen says.

“We could tell that was going to be the first song on the album as soon as we wrote it,” Cherry adds. “When it feels right, you can tell, because we just want to play the song again and again and again.”.

Industry observers note that others emerged more fully-formed, like “Still Angry,” which came from a voice note that Leppänen sent the band. “I played it to my mom,” Ward indicates. “I was like, ‘Listen to this shit. It’s a fucking amazing pop song. Vera’s done it again.'”.

It has been revealed that “Nosedive” came into focus near the end of the sessions. “We needed a couple more songs for our album, and we took names out of a hat and split into two groups,” Starwood recalls. In one room, the three lead singers — Leppänen, Ward, and Avery — wrote a vocal part by reworking an acoustic demo that Avery had brought in. In another, the three remaining members put together an instrumental arrangement that’s slower and softer than most Chainsaw songs, and entirely enchanting.

According to recent reports, “We spent the rest of the evening just jamming it,” notes Starwood, who remembers holding down a synth note with one foot while her hands were busy on violin. “It came together in such a satisfying way.”.

Recent findings suggest that last winter, as they were putting the finishing touches on the album, several of the bandmates met in the studio to record backing vocals for the song. A few days later, after speaking with some students back at the BRIT School, Cherry heard the new mix with those group vocals for the first time. “It was so full-circle,” the drummer recalls. “It was so sweet. Tears in my eyes.”.

“Nosedive” remains a highlight at their live highlights, and they generally save it for the last spot in the set list. “Billy Ward’s dad got him for Christmas a bubble gun in the shape of a pink chainsaw, and Vera always wields it in that song,” Starwood indicates.

Sources indicate that at a recent hometown gig at London’s Electric Ballroom, they took that peak even higher by detonating a confetti cannon during “Nosedive.” “It was a substantial bang,” Starwood says. “It was really loud.”.

It has been revealed that that does raise a potential problem for their reveals next year, which include another run of bigger U.S. clubs in Fresh York, Boston, Philadelphia, Austin, and Washington, D.C. in February.

“I don’t know how you top bubbles coming out of a pink chainsaw and confetti,” Starwood continues. “We can’t do the same thing twice. Dancers, maybe?” Trending Stories Watch Buffalo Springfield Come Together for the First Time in Many Years Jennifer Lopez Teases New Music on ‘Fallon’: ‘This Does Feel Like a Happy Era’ The ‘You Can See Everything’ Interview You’ve Been Waiting For Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters Files for Divorce From Fourth Wife Kamilah Chavis After 5 Years of Marriage.

“Pyrotechnics,” Ward says. “That’s the word of the year, 2027: pyrotechnics.”.

For anyone building a premium home theater around a large TV, the Sony Bravia Theater Trio is down to $1,498 from $2,199.99, saving you $701.99, or roughly 32%. Unlike a conventional soundbar, the Trio uses three separate front speakers for the left, center, and right channels, helping spread dialogue and effects across a wider soundstage. You can read PCMag’s “excellent” review for more details.

The Sony Bravia Theater Bar 7 is down to $718 from $869 for anyone who wants a single soundbar under the TV. Its nine speakers include upward- and side-firing drivers that widen the soundstage and give Dolby Atmos some height, but there’s no subwoofer, so the now $898 Bar 7 with a wireless sub bundle (down from $1,099.99) might be the better pick for deeper bass.

According to recent reports, moving down Sony's lineup, the Bravia Theater Bar 6 is $548, down from $699.99, and pairs a 3.1.2-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer and upward-firing speakers for Dolby Atmos height effects. Spending $100 more gets you the Bravia Theater System 6, now $648 from $799.99, which adds rear speakers in a 5.1-channel setup for movies and games where sound moves behind you.

For a more affordable upgrade, the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 5 is down to $278 from $349.99, saving you nearly $72. It's a 3.1-channel system with a dedicated center speaker and wireless subwoofer, so dialogue should come through more clearly while music and movie effects get some additional low-end presence.

Sony’s older systems are discounted too, including the HT-S400 at $258, down from $299, which pairs a 2.1-channel soundbar and wireless subwoofer with S-Force Pro Front Surround to widen the sound for everyday TV, sports, and casual movies. The HT-S40R is arguably the better deal at the same $258, down from $329.99, since it adds two rear speakers for a full 5.1-channel setup, though neither model supports Dolby Atmos.

For smaller rooms or for anyone who mainly wants dialogue to come across more clearly, Bose has two compact soundbars on sale: The newer Bose TV Speaker (2nd Gen) is down to $239 from $299, with an updated acoustic design that Bose says improves clarity and overall sound performance. Meanwhile, the original Bose TV Speaker is $199, down from $279, and offers a similarly compact design with a dedicated dialogue mode and adjustable bass.

It has been revealed that samsung’s HW-Q800H is down to $697.99 from $1,097.99, a $400 cut on a 5.1.2-channel Dolby Atmos soundbar with a wireless subwoofer. Its side- and upward-firing speakers help place effects around and above you, while a dedicated center channel keeps dialogue clear during busy action scenes.

Industry observers note that for something that takes up less space, the Samsung HW-S60D is $277.99, down from $399.99, and fits seven speakers, including side-firing drivers, into a compact 5.0-channel soundbar. It also supports Dolby Atmos, Adaptive Sound, and a voice enhancement mode, along with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, AirPlay, and Chromecast for music streaming. That noted, it has no upward-firing speakers or subwoofer, so its height effects and bass won’t match that of the Q800H.

In a recent development, if you're looking for a complete surround sound system without spending several hundred dollars, the LG S6FTR is down to $249.99 from $399.99, saving you $150, or roughly 38%. It's a 5.1-channel home theater package with a soundbar, subwoofer, and dedicated rear speakers. It has been revealed that the LG S40TR is another affordable option for anyone who wants rear speakers included in the box. It's currently $199.99, down from $279.99, and offers a 4.1-channel arrangement with a wireless subwoofer and two rear speakers. This should give movie soundtracks a greater sense of direction than a basic soundbar, while the subwoofer handles the lower frequencies that smaller TV speakers often struggle to reproduce.

Recent findings suggest that at just under $187, the S60T is the least expensive system in this roundup, pairing a 3.1-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer for clearer dialogue and fuller sound than your TV’s speakers. That noted, it lacks rear speakers and Dolby Atmos height channels, so it’s better suited to someone who wants a simple, affordable upgrade without filling the room with additional hardware.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

In a recent development, black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

Tech Report: Epic formally asks SCOTUS to uphold contempt ruling against Apple

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that epic Games has submitted its official response to Apple’s Supreme Court appeal, urging the justices to uphold the contempt ruling over App Store payment restrictions.
  • As most 9to5Mac readers probably know, Apple and Epic Games have been engaged in a lengthy legal battle since 2020, when Epic sued Apple after Fortnite was removed from the App Store.
  • The move came after Epic remotely activated an alternative payment system that bypassed Apple’s In-App Purchase system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that epic Games has submitted its official response to Apple’s Supreme Court appeal, urging the justices to uphold the contempt ruling over App Store payment restrictions. Here are the details.

As most 9to5Mac readers probably know, Apple and Epic Games have been engaged in a lengthy legal battle since 2020, when Epic sued Apple after Fortnite was removed from the App Store.

The move came after Epic remotely activated an alternative payment system that bypassed Apple’s In-App Purchase system.

Although the court largely sided with Apple, it did rule that the company could no longer prevent developers from directing customers to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.

Apple ultimately allowed those links, but imposed new restrictions, including a 27% commission on external purchases, in addition to new rules limiting how developers could display buttons and links to alternative payment methods.

Epic challenged those restrictions, and the court agreed that Apple had violated the original injunction, holding the manufacturer in civil contempt.

Apple has since attempted multiple times to overturn that ruling, arguing that the original injunction contained no explicit prohibition on imposing those restrictions.

Epic, on the other hand, argues that Apple deliberately circumvented the court order by introducing newly introduced rules designed to achieve the same result as those originally prohibited.

In May, Apple appealed to the Supreme Court, which agreed in June to hear the case. Apple submitted its opening brief in September, followed by supporting briefs from the U.S. government and several legal and business groups.

Those included the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Chamber of Progress, and several former federal antitrust enforcers. In a nutshell, the U.S. government argued that the original injunction did not clearly prohibit Apple’s 27% commission on external purchases, but maintained that the manufacturer was correctly held in contempt for restricting how developers could display external payment buttons.

Today, Epic filed its official response.

In its opening brief, Apple argues, citing multiple legal precedents, that courts must enforce the letter of an injunction rather than its broader spirit.

According to the organization, there was nothing in the original injunction explicitly prohibiting it from charging commissions on external purchases or imposing additional restrictions on payment links, so it should not be held in contempt for conduct that the court order did not clearly prohibit.

In its response filed today, Epic disputes Apple’s interpretation of the injunction, arguing that the manufacturer “attempts to avoid contempt by proposing an extreme legal standard.”.

According to recent reports, [Apple] argues that a court can find contempt only if an injunction spells out the exact practice at matter–so an injunction barring Apple’s then-existing anti-steering rules left it free to implement upcoming ones that prevent steering just as effectively. Nothing in this Court’s precedents supports that approach, which would reduce injunctions to a never-ending game of whack-a-mole.

Epic argues that “Apple devised a plan to circumvent the injunction,” claiming that “Apple chose a rate of 27% for the commission, knowing that, when combined with the developers’ payment-handling costs (more than 3%), the rate for linked-out purchases would be higher than the rate for purchases using Apple’s payment system.”.

As an Apple executive admitted, every “linked-out transaction is going to be more expensive to any developer * * * than an IAP transaction at 30 percent.” Apple simultaneously commissioned a “sham” report to try to provide an economic justification for the commission; the report contained an “entirely manufactured” rationale for the 27% rate.

The company also argues that “Apple tried to cover up its scheme to circumvent the injunction” by asserting privilege over more than 57,000 documents, and points to Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers’ finding that “its Vice President of Finance ‘outright lied under oath’ when he testified about when Apple decided to impose the upcoming commission.”.

Finally, Epic asks the Supreme Court to uphold the contempt ruling against Apple or, if the justices decide to clarify the legal standard for contempt, to send the case back to the lower courts for reconsideration under that standard.

With Epic’s response now filed, Apple has until December 14 to submit its final brief before oral arguments take place on January 11, 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • When I first published this article on Thursday, I couldn't even load Microsoft 365's status page.
  • Looking specifically at Outlook, Microsoft's email service had hundreds of thousands of user reports Thursday afternoon, signaling a major matter somewhere in Microsoft's pipeline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you were having trouble accessing certain services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook, you were not alone. Early Thursday afternoon, many of Microsoft's biggest apps and services were experiencing downtime. According to Downdetector, which tracks user reports of issues with websites and platforms, Microsoft 365, Teams, Copilot, Teams, and OneDrive were all experiencing issues. As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft has restored service to many customers, and has officially apologized for the outages.

When I first published this article on Thursday, I couldn't even load Microsoft 365's status page. (I've reported on many service outages, but I can't recall a time when a service's status page was also down.) Even as of Friday afternoon, the page still indicates "Service degradation on Microsoft 365 (Business or Enterprise)," and Microsoft says the following services may be affected: Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center, Microsoft 365 Education, Microsoft Copilot 365, Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Graph, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Planner, Microsoft Power Apps, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft To Do, Power BI, SharePoint Online, Universal Print, and Windows 365.

Looking specifically at Outlook, Microsoft's email service had hundreds of thousands of user reports Thursday afternoon, signaling a major matter somewhere in Microsoft's pipeline. The reports did "slow down" throughout the day, but Downdetector still showed over 50,000 reports coming in every 15 minutes when I checked Thursday afternoon.

While the root cause of the issue was a mystery throughout Thursday's outage, Microsoft confirmed the problem in an apology on Friday. According to the firm, "This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI [or] agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.".

Microsoft claims it is "deeply sorry" for the disruption to its customers and partners. The organization says the fix rolled out slower than some might expect, since it wanted to restore service gradually to evaluate stability at each stage. It also says it will release a full post-incident report once it completes a review.

In a recent development, during the outage, the company had confirmed that some of its infrastructure was experiencing elevated load, which it mentioned was likely contributing to the concerns. Microsoft then said it was pausing all deployments and moving traffic from affected infrastructure, and that it found that a number of its servers were unexpectedly unavailable after failing health checks. The company then thought a specific component responsible for processing server health may be the reason the system is failing health checks. Microsoft said an alternative service health check method successfully restarted some of the affected servers. The company was then actively restarting and validating affected servers to bring them back to service.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We partnered with Baseten to build the largest-scale harness leaderboard using 83B tokens across 27,280 agent runs. We wanted to answer two questions: when you switch your model, should you consider switching the harness too? What is the best harness for each model?

Previously, our v1.0 FrontierHarness leaderboard ranked harnesses on a single model, Kimi K3.

V1.1 expands the benchmark to 22 harnesses Ã 5 models Ã 62 tasks Ã 4 attempts, 76Ã the size of v1.0.

Through our experiments, we found that you should consider switching harnesses when switching models to maximize your experience.

Industry observers note that each model had a different best-value (pass rate vs. cost) harness: Codex CLI with GLM-5.3, Pi with GLM-5.3 Flash, ZCode with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, Oh My Pi with Muse and Alma with Kimi-K3. Cost ranks moved far between models.

By cost per task, the median harness moved 11 of 22 places, and Codex CLI went from 1st with GLM-5.3 to 16th with Kimi-K3.

Each card names the best-value harness for one model: the lowest cost per pass, unless another harness costs at most 30% more per pass and passes at least 5 points more often. This rule picked ZCode over OpenCode v1 with DeepSeek (25% more cost, 7.7 more points) and Alma over Oh My Pi with Kimi-K3 (9% more cost, 6.5 more points).

Industry observers note that V1.0 ran nine harnesses with one model. Their pass rates were within 17 points of each other, but the median cost per pass differed by 17 times. We thought that this came mostly from the pair of harness and model: a harness that is cheap with one model can be expensive with another.

Recent findings suggest that put in franchise perspective, GTA VI’s pre-order haul is just a touch under double the launch of the $800 million snared by 2013’s Grand Theft Auto V, the previous all-time entertainment debut record holder. GTA V, which like GTA VI was pushed back from its originally stated release date, has gone on to sell more than 235 million units. The sometimes grisly GTA V has also proved a massive hit on publisher Rockstar Games‘ lucrative GTA Online multiplayer platform.

To give you an idea of the massive numbers in store here for GTA VI‘s first day when it comes to the big screen, the global box office opening day alone this year on Sony/Marvel Studio’s Spider-Man: Brand Newly introduced Day was $276.1 million (note that some foreign territories open on Wednesday and Thursday and have their ticket sales rolled into North America’s opening day Friday). Five movies have grossed over $1 billion worldwide year-to-date, Brand New Day being the highest at $2.5 billion, ahead of The Odyssey ($1.8 billion), Toy Story ($1.1 billion), biopic Michael ($1 billion) and Super Mario Galaxy Movie ($1 billion).

According to recent reports, at the current trajectory leading to GTA VI going live at midnight local time globally on November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, pre-orders are on target to hit sales of 20 million and $2 billion in revenue before the end of the week. Before the end of the year, with day of launch purchases and then holiday shopping factoring in, GTA IV is estimated to bring in around $3 billion, indicates L.A.-based Wedbush Securities.

Sources indicate that “Next to James Bond, there might not be another franchise of this scale that has been as consistent with its brand,” says Larry Vincent, professor of Marketing at USC Marshall School of Business. “It’s like they apprenticed with the Broccali family,” he adds of the Take-Two Interactive owned series and the former 007 bosses.

In a recent development, kinder and gentler in execution than past sex worker killing and explicit content containing installments of the 1997 originating open sandbox franchise, the still very violent GTA VI finds the detail rich immersive series returning to the Miami-inspired Vice City. Which means, much like 2002’s single player Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, the ever-expanding crime escapades of lovers Jason and Lucia in this iteration are neon streaked, car chase fueled, bullet loaded and blood soaked in the sweaty fictional state of Leonida.

In a recent development, filled to the brim with a satirical and scathing take on American culture. GTA VI is clearly giving the people the blood and circus they want.

Add to that, as Sony put out last minute PS5 software updates, a worry for later in the week is that the internet could slow due to spike in YouTube livestreams and social media posts as players drill into the game.

Industry observers note that A true global release, GTA VI nearly crashed Netflix this summer with its well watched Extended Look featurette. As proof of the streamer’s own clout and reach, GTA VI pre-sales surged once the 27-minute Extended Look dropped on August 27.

In a recent development, with skyscrapers, hoardings and murals all over the seven continents displaying GTA VI artwork, product activations soared. Songs from the game has topped playlists too, with a soundtrack score by electronic duo Justice out on December 11.

They fell 4% on Tuesday and are now down 20% in 2026 to date as Wall Street has sought to reconcile the runaway success of the GTA franchise with decidedly mixed quarterly financial results. Take-Two aren’t the only ones feeling the pinch. All video game publishers have been scrambling of late to adjust to an evolving consumer marketplace, with mobile and casual games meaningfully eating into the share of traditional console tentpoles.

With that, any deeper bottom line comparisons between MAGA era GTA VI and the Obama Era GTA V does become a little bit apples to avocados.

To frustration of some, the 2026 game is only available digitally as opposed to on the more traditional disc of previous GTAs. Which is also why, if you are a gamer or gamer adjacent, you have spent days over the past week downloading the colossal 212GB GTA VI for Thursday’s debut. In anticipation of November 19, which is widely viewed as an adult snow day with millions of fans playing hooky off work to play the game, you may have also been forking out more cash to upgrading your console so you can play GTA VI in either its $79.99 Standard Edition or the $99.99 Ultimate Edition.

It is that money pit mentality from the video game industry that spurned Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY) to put the Power to the Players Act before Congress last month. Still collecting co-sponsors and paused a bit as a newly Democratic-controlled majority prepares to take power, the P2P Act would compel the FCC to ensure that buying a game means it’s the consumer’s, full stop.

“Just based on revenue, the video game industry is larger than global film, global music, and North American sports combined,” the just re-elected South Bronx representing Democrat indicates. “It’s massive, and historically, it’s been the most affordable form of entertainment,” the Congressman asserts. “My district is hit the hardest by the affordability crisis, and digital-only distribution disproportionately disadvantages the lowest-income consumers, who are more likely to trade and use games to subsidize the purchase of upcoming ones.”.

Sources indicate that in a stance that runs counter to where Take-Two and much of the industry are taking things, Rep. Torrs adds: “My view is that in a properly functioning marketplace, when you pay for a video game, you should be purchasing the game itself, right? If you pay for it, then you should own it. Simple rule, but increasingly, when you pay for a video game, you are not purchasing the game itself. You are purchasing a license to play the game, and that license can be revoked arbitrarily at the discretion of the gaming manufacturer. So, it feels to me like we as consumers are paying higher and higher prices while enjoying fewer and fewer rights, if any rights at all.”.

Torres’ bill has a way to go before becoming a law, but it is certainly now part of the cultural conversation sparked by GTA VI‘s mega-release As close to a monoculture moment as we can have in 2026, GTA VI is a conversation even the cops and the Weather Channel have joined:.

It has been revealed that GTA is not a real place, but Atlanta is!🎮Don't confuse virtual entertainment with real-life decisions.Drunk driving, reckless driving, auto theft and violence have real consequences.Keep it in the game. Don't bring it to our streets. pic.twitter.com/Y7PdJFHLsZ.

Looks like we have to add Vice City as a location on our app…🌴👀.

Another voice in all this belongs to producer and actor Matthew Waterson. Best known as the voice of X-Men ’97‘s Magneto, Waterson is also an alum of the blockbuster Call of Duty franchise and Rockstar’s best selling Red Dead Redemption games.

“They’re such unique properties that people are willing to wait for, people are willing to talk about, think about it and get excited for because they build such rich environments,” Waterson insists of GTA and RDR. “Most other companies at this point don’t have the the time or the money or the capital to do that,”.

“These big public companies don’t have the capital expenditure abilities to put 10 years into a huge world concept game if they don’t know it’s going to make money,” indicates Waterson of risk adverse and cash restricted studios and streamers. “Rockstar have two products that they know are going to make money. Rockstar can do that, and just about nobody else can.”.

Anthony D’Alessandro & Dade Hayes contributed to this report.

10 Books Like ‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ You Should Read Next

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1298 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Maas’ lush, romance-soaked series A Court of Thorns and Roses has blossomed into a sprawling, complex fantasy series with millions of dedicated fans, and with good reason.
  • Industry observers note that the story of a huntress who is kidnapped by a fae prince and brought to the Spring Court as a prisoner, only to become a key player in all that fae drama, ACOTAR is special, but Maas can only write so fast.
  • Maas’ other series would be recommended for fans of A Court of Thorns and Roses, but there’s a specific reason you should jump into her Crescent City series, especially the third book, House of Flame and Shadow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sarah J. Maas’ lush, romance-soaked series A Court of Thorns and Roses has blossomed into a sprawling, complex fantasy series with millions of dedicated fans, and with good reason. A complex heroine who keeps discovering newly introduced depths in herself, fascinating supporting characters who shift from antihero to antivillain in unexpected ways, creative and beautifully rendered world-building—the series has it all, while also being unapologetically romantic (and steamy).

Industry observers note that the story of a huntress who is kidnapped by a fae prince and brought to the Spring Court as a prisoner, only to become a key player in all that fae drama, ACOTAR is special, but Maas can only write so fast. If you need more books with the same lush feel, here are 10 to get you started.

It’s no shock that one of Sarah J. Maas’ other series would be recommended for fans of A Court of Thorns and Roses, but there’s a specific reason you should jump into her Crescent City series, especially the third book, House of Flame and Shadow. The most recent ACOTAR book, A Court of Splintered Harmony, revealed that the events of House of Flame and Shadow tie directly into the events in Splintered Harmony, particularly with regard to the character of Feyre’s sister, Nesta. In other words, if you read Splintered Harmony and wondered why Nesta was being so weird, there’s a whole other book series you should dig into immediately.

According to recent reports, if Feyre’s grit and determination are your favorite aspect of ACOTAR, Julie Kagawa’s Iron Fey series (starting with The Iron King) will be your next obsession. Meghan Chase has never felt ‘normal’ in her life, and she’s been haunted by her father’s disappearance since she was a child. When her brother also vanishes, she goes on a quest for answers, learns that she’s actually the daughter of a faerie king, and finds herself in a magical world that blurs in elements of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream. Meghan is determined to save her brother (and herself), but a certain ice-cold fae prince captures her attention, even though he’s as dangerous as he is beautiful.

If you’re looking for some serious romance in your fantasy, Jennifer L. Armentrout’s A Blood and Ash series is a must. Poppy was chosen at birth to be the kingdom’s Maiden, isolated and untouched in order to be ready for her Ascension to ensure the land is protected from the evil force that took her family. But it’s a lonely existence—until Hawke is assigned as her sworn protector. Golden-eyed and beautiful, Hawke offers Poppy the connection she’s craved. When chaos erupts around her, Hawke takes the opportunity to spirit Poppy away. But Hawke has a secret, and Poppy is soon in danger of losing both her heart and the favor of the gods themselves.

If you love how A Court of Thorns and Roses takes the “enemies-to-lovers” trope and builds it into a deep, complex mesh of emotions and plot twists, you’ll love Shelby Mahurin’s Serpent & Dove series. When witch Louise le Blanc flees her coven, she takes shelter in the city of Cesarine, where magic is forbidden, and witches are unceremoniously hunted and burned. Louise’s life gets infinitely more complicated, dangerous, and steamy when she’s trapped into an unwanted marriage with Reid Diggory—who happens to be a huntsman of the Church, charged with tracking down and eliminating witches. And then Louise starts to realize that Reid is actually pretty darn hot.

If you’re looking for a romantasy that’s broadly similar to ACOTAR while being its own thing, read A.K. Mulford’s The Five Crowns of Okrith series, starting with The High Mountain Court. Remy is a red witch, which means she’s in hiding and ready to make a run for it if the fae get near. So when a group of fae indicates up at her tavern, she makes for the exit—only to be captured by Prince Hale of the Eastern Court. Instead of striking her down, however, Hale asks Remy for help—he needs to locate two ancient magical artifacts created by red witches, and he needs her red magic to find them. Hale promises to set her free and even reunite her with the red witches still living. More importantly, Remy finds Hale irresistible and has a primal urge to stay with him, no matter what the cost.

It has been revealed that looking for a romantasy with a slightly different vibe from ACOTAR? Variety is the spice of life, after all—and The Fourth Wing delivers. Rebecca Yarros’ Empyrean Series made a huge splash when it debuted, and for good reason—it has everything, from a capable, intelligent heroine thrust into a dangerous scenario (in this case, a dragon rider academy where failure can be deadly) and forced to navigate alliances, conspiracies, and her own heart, which is pushing her towards a romance that might be as dangerous as the dragons themselves.

According to recent reports, love the moral complexity of ACOTAR, where everyone has at least a touch of darkness? Check out The Folk of the Air series by Holly Black. When Jude was a child, the father of her half-sister, the faerie Madoc, murdered her parents and took her back to the Faerie world with him. Raised as part of the gentry, Jude lives in a world where her mortal nature is hated and despised, but she battles for her place at court anyway while struggling with her love-hate relationship with her adoptive father and a growing bond with the titular prince, a relationship that is strictly forbidden. Jude is a fierce and extremely morally gray character, and one that fans of Feyre will adore.

Industry observers note that looking for more smart women at the center of beautifully-rendered fantasy stories? You’ll love Princess Lucero-Elisa de Riqueza of Orovalle, star of this series-starter by Rae Carson. Elisa was chosen for “Service” as a baby, when a godstone was placed in her navel by the gods, signaling that she was destined for greatness. But as a young woman, Elisa is self-hating and miserable. She’s never done anything even remotely great, and spends her time isolated, overweight, and reading military strategy books. One day she’s shocked to discover she’s been married off to the king of a distant land on the brink of war—and suddenly all that rage and book learning becomes invaluable as she struggles to survive an unfamiliar court and help her newly introduced homeland survive a dangerous onslaught.

If you loved Feyre’s journey as she discovered unknown reservoirs of power and courage inside herself, you should read Leigh Bardugo’s Grishaverse novels, starting with Shadow and Bone. As a child, Alina was tested by the Grisha and found to possess no magical ability. As an adult, she serves as a cartographer in the army. Charged with guiding the Darkling—the most powerful of the Grisha—across the dangerous and terrifying Shadow Fold, Alina is unexpectedly revealed to have incredible powers and is packed off to train with the Grisha. There, she must determine who her friends and enemies are, even while falling under the spell of the charismatic Darkling.

Emilia di Carlo and her sister Vittoria are very different—Emilia is bookish and shy, Vittoria outgoing and brash—but they share a secret: They’re both streghe, and have spent their lives learning to use magic. In this version of Italy, the Malvagi (the seven princes of Hell) haven’t been seen in a long time, but a terrifying accident summons the Prince of Wrath and leaves three witches dead, including Vittoria. Emilia swears to use her power to avenge her sister, but when her revenge is delayed and she’s forced to work with Wrath, unwanted feelings begin to tick up the spice level to an uncomfortable degree.

Industry News: Tired of paying for cloud storage every month? pCloud’s Black Friday Lifetime deal is the cure for subscription fatigue

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1065 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that software used to be a one-time purchase, but over time, with the addition of cloud storage and services, everything has become a subscription.
  • According to recent reports, everything is a service now, and a lot of people are hitting the point where one more monthly charge is one too many on principle alone.
  • Industry observers note that apple gives you 5 GB of iCloud for free, which stops being enough about a week after you buy an iPhone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that software used to be a one-time purchase, but over time, with the addition of cloud storage and services, everything has become a subscription. One firm even tried to make your car seat heaters a subscription. Count the subscriptions you’re paying for right now: iCloud, a password manager, a couple of streaming services, a music service, maybe a VPN, and whatever other app decided this year that it needed to be $4.99 per month for something that used to be a one-time purchase.

According to recent reports, everything is a service now, and a lot of people are hitting the point where one more monthly charge is one too many on principle alone. Cloud storage is the one that’s hardest to cancel, because your photos and files are in it. That’s exactly why pCloud’s Lifetime intends are worth a look this Black Friday: you pay once, and your storage is yours for life!

Industry observers note that apple gives you 5 GB of iCloud for free, which stops being enough about a week after you buy an iPhone. The irony is that they launched with 5 GB of free storage in 2011, and it’s almost laughable that it hasn’t been increased since.

After that, it’s a subscription forever. The 2 TB iCloud+ initiative costs $9.99 a month, about $120 a year, for as long as you want your photos to stay where they are. pCloud’s math is different. The 2 TB Lifetime plan is a one-time payment that costs less than four years of iCloud+ at the same size, and the day you buy it is the last day you pay anything for it.

pCloud has offered lifetime intends for 9 years and now 24 million people use it, and it’s run by a Swiss firm under Swiss privacy law. The “what if they go away” question is fair for any lifetime offer, and a company with that track record is the best answer you’re going to get.

If you’ve been paying for iCloud or Google Drive storage for all of your files for the last 9 years instead of using pCloud, go do the math on how much you’ve spent.

It has been revealed that apple charges a lot to move from a 256 GB MacBook Air to a 512 GB one, and you can’t change your mind later with a hard drive upgrade. Storage has gotten incredibly pricey in recent years as well. pCloud Drive is your solution without breaking the bank. It’s a native Mac app that mounts your pCloud storage as a drive in Finder, so your files appear as if they’re natively on your Mac but live in the cloud until you open them. A 256 GB laptop with a 2 TB pCloud Drive behind it stops feeling small. It runs on macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android, and everything stays in sync across all of them in real time.

Sources indicate that with pCloud Backup, backing up the folders you choose is easy and safe from a lost laptop, fire, flood, or theft. If you run a NAS at home, pCloud supports backing it up via WebDAV, Rsync, SFTP, and SCP, making it a real offsite destination for a Synology NAS, not just a simple sync folder. It would be a perfect offsite backup for small businesses, remote workers, etc.

Sources indicate that iCloud Photos is great, but it uses storage from your iCloud storage quota, which can get expensive as Apple’s cameras get better and better and file sizes keep increasing. Every pCloud plan includes pCloud Photos, a photo gallery that organizes everything by date on a timeline, automatically tags objects and scenes, and groups shots into albums by event and person.

The pCloud mobile app backs up your camera roll automatically to free up space on your iPhone; a Memories feature resurfaces older photos, as the Photos app does; and a built-in document scanner turns receipts and paperwork into PDFs without needing a separate app. Inside the app, there is also a built-in Photo Editor with crop, rotate, brightness, contrast, highlights, shadows, and eight one-click filters, so quick fixes don’t require moving it back to Apple Photos.

pCloud Docs covers documents, spreadsheets, presentations, PDFs, text, and markdown with six built-in editors and real-time collaboration, all from the browser or the mobile app. If your household is split, with one person on Microsoft, Apple, or Google, pCloud can pull in files from Google Photos, Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, and Facebook. That’s the easiest way I’ve seen to get everyone’s files into one place without needing to download and reupload everything.

Files and photos aren’t the only benefit of joining the pCloud ecosystem. pCloud Pass is a password manager that works across all devices, browsers, and operating systems, with one-click login, form filling, and a generator for strong, unique passwords. Passwords are still hard, and most people are either paying monthly for a manager or reusing the same three passwords. A lifetime license solves the annoying aspects of using a dedicated password manager app or being locked into Apple’s or Google’s systems.

Sources indicate that pCloud Encryption is client-side, zero-knowledge encryption for your most sensitive files. In plain language: files in your Crypto folder are encrypted on your Mac before they upload, and only you hold the key. pCloud can’t read them, and neither can anyone else. It’s the right place for tax returns, scans of your birth certificate, and anything else you’d rather not have sitting in a regular sync folder.

#27758. Tech Report: Solid 2.0
